acl:2026.sigul-1.8.title: Urdu-CLEVR: A Novel Benchmark for Visual Reasoning in an Under-Resourced Linguistic Context
acl:2026.sigul-1.8.venue: Proceedings of the SIGUL 2026 Joint Workshop with ELE, EURALI, and DCLRL: Towards Inclusivity and Equality: Language Resources and Technologies for Under-Resourced and Endangered Languages

acl:2026.slide-1.10.abstract: This paper presents a two-stage training approach to improve the performance of Slovene large language models on lexicographic question-answering tasks. We developed a comprehensive lexical pretraining corpus containing 356,294 Slovene word entries. We constructed the corpus by converting structured data from multiple lexicographic sources into markdown format. Additionally, we created a question-answering dataset with 10,485 QA pairs from diverse sources, including automatically generated questions, a linguistic advisory portal, and community forums. Using the Slovenian GaMS model (based on Gemma 2 9B) and GaMS 3 model (based on Gemma 3 12B), we performed continued pretraining on the lexical corpus, followed by instruction fine-tuning with our QA dataset combined with translated general-domain questions. We compared results to different model configurations. Our results demonstrate significant improvements (text similarity increasing from 0.226 to 0.542, BERTScore F1 of 0.915) in answering Slovene lexicographic questions, validating the effectiveness of domain-specific continued pretraining for low-resource languages.
acl:2026.slide-1.10.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Workshop on Structured Linguistic Data and Evaluation (SLiDE)
acl:2026.slide-1.10.title: Improving Slovene Language Models for Lexicographic Question Answering through Continued Pretraining and Instruction Fine-Tuning
acl:2026.slide-1.10.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Structured Linguistic Data and Evaluation (SLiDE)

acl:2026.speakable-1.14.abstract: Multi-modal Speech Language Models (SpeechLMs) are a recent advancement in natural language processing. These SpeechLMs are instruction-tuned and optimized for general tasks. Their usefulness for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), particularly in relatively low-resource scenarios, remains largely understudied. This work developed SpeechLM for ASR in Basque and Maltese and studied the impact of language-adapted Large Language Model (LLM) and speech encoder within the SpeechLM for ASR. Using supervised learning, we fine-tuned LLaMA-Omni, a SpeechLM, for ASR. We have conducted comprehensive hyperparameter tuning and experimented with language-adapted SpeechLM components to improve performance and evaluated our best models on in-distribution datasets for both languages and an out-of-distribution dataset for Basque. LLaMA-Omni achieved 8.09% WER in Basque and 25.65% WER for Maltese on average across multiple test splits. The in-distribution results show that SpeechLM outperforms a fine-tuned ASR system under specific constraints, whereas it underperforms the baseline model on out-of-distribution Basque, indicating weaker overall robustness. We also find that a language-adapted LLM within SpeechLM improves in out-of-distribution settings when compared to the off-the-shelf LLM within SpeechLM.
acl:2026.speakable-1.14.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.speakable-1.14.title: SpeechLM for Automatic Speech Recognition in Low-resource Languages
acl:2026.speakable-1.14.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.15.abstract: This study explores how bilingual fine-tuning affects automatic speech recognition (ASR) in low-resource languages. We evaluate this method across nine linguistically and geographically diverse language pairs, covering a range of language families and writing systems. To distinguish the two languages, during training, we pre-pend each input text with a language identification token. At inference, the model jointly predicts both the language and transcription from the speech input alone. As texts for which the language is incorrectly determined show low ASR performance, we also conduct a follow-up experiment in which the language identification token is provided both during training and inference. Our results show that bilingual fine-tuning can be beneficial when language identification accuracy is high, and that in cases where language identification performance is low, including the language identification token at inference helps to improve ASR performance.
acl:2026.speakable-1.15.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.speakable-1.15.title: Improving Low-resource ASR Using Bilingual Fine-tuning with Language Identification: A Cross-linguistic Evaluation
acl:2026.speakable-1.15.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.16.abstract: This study presents our attempt on applying Query by Example - Spoken Term Detection methodologies to a real-world, low-resource scenario: building an audio-based query functionality for the diasporan Teochew dictionary WhatTCSay. This functionality enables users to retrieve dictionary entries without prior knowledge of the writing systems in Teochew, thereby enhancing the accessibility of the dictionary and facilitating language revitalization efforts within Teochew communities. To address the retrieval task, we investigate two approaches: (i) an ASR-based approach using text-to-text matching, and (ii) a Dynamic Time Warping (DTW)-based acoustic framework for audio-to-audio retrieval. In the first approach, we compare an automatic romanization of the spoken query against the gold romanization from the dictionary; in the second, we directly match the user’s spoken query against audio recordings from the dictionary pronounced by a native speaker. Retrieval performance is evaluated using recall at rank k. Results show that text-to-text matching achieves better performance than audio-to-audio matching; however, the two approaches were not optimized under fully comparable conditions, as the ASR-based approach benefited from additional optimization, which was not equally available for the DTW method.
acl:2026.speakable-1.16.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.speakable-1.16.title: Leveraging Speech Models for Audio-based Lexical Retrieval in Dictionaries: The Case of the Teochew Language
acl:2026.speakable-1.16.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.17.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) for low-resource languages remains challenging due to limited labeled data. Although multilingual models and the inclusion of related auxiliary languages enable cross-lingual transfer, it is still unclear how introducing cross-lingual information at different training stages-pre-training versus fine-tuning-affects downstream performance. Prior work largely treats transfer as a single-stage optimization problem without disentangling stage effects. We present a stage-aware analysis of cross-lingual transfer for Faroese ASR using related auxiliary languages and Wav2Vec 2.0 XLS-R models. We systematically compare two complementary adaptation pipelines: (i) cross-lingual supervised fine-tuning and (ii) cross-lingual continuous pre-training prior to fine-tuning. Both strategies are evaluated under a unified setup with controlled model architectures, balanced representation of auxiliary languages, and identical evaluation protocols. Results demonstrate that cross-lingual transfer is stage-dependent. Supervised adaptation optimizes in-domain accuracy, while pretraining-level adaptation enhances robustness and reduces Character Error Rate (CER). Auxiliary language effects vary across pipelines, reinforcing the idea that transfer effectiveness depends on when and how cross-lingual information is introduced. Comparisons with large-scale multilingual ASR models highlight trade-offs between model scale and explicit, small-scale domain-aware adaptation. These findings suggest that effective cross-lingual transfer for Faroese low-resource ASR is inherently stage-dependent rather than a single-step design choice.
acl:2026.speakable-1.17.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.speakable-1.17.title: Stage-Aware Cross-Lingual Transfer for Faroese ASR: When and Which Languages Matter
acl:2026.speakable-1.17.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.18.abstract: In recent years, there has been an upsurge in research on automatic speech recognition (ASR) for low-resource languages. Particularly, transfer learning using multi-lingual models has become a popular remedy for the lack of available datasets for target languages. However, given the complexities associated with each individual language, we argue it is unlikely that a single multi-lingual pre-training model will provide equal performance gains across all languages. We also recognise the important, and insufficiently studied influence that the specific pre-training dataset has on the performance of the model. In this paper, using the Irish language as a case study, we propose a more directed, incremental form of pre-training which we term multi-step fine-tuning. This method accounts for the complex relationships between the language and dataset features of the source pre-training and target datasets. We show multi-step fine-tuning improves performance over simple multi-lingual fine-tuning alone, and we investigate factors leading to certain pre-trained models achieving better results through linguistic and dataset similarity measures. This research also investigates the uniformity of the performance gains across different demographics. We show that the optimal pre-training strategy can differ between demographics suggesting that more careful pre-training dataset selection is necessary to ensure equitable outcomes in practice.
acl:2026.speakable-1.18.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.speakable-1.18.title: Doing More with Less: Determining Optimal Pre-training Model for Irish Automatic Speech Recognition through Multi-step Fine-tuning
acl:2026.speakable-1.18.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.speakable-1.19.abstract: We present a blank-aware decoding approach for transcript-free phoneme alignment with CTC-based speech foundation models, designed to improve annotation bootstrapping in low-resource languages. While CTC models provide frame-level phoneme posteriors without requiring transcripts, greedy decoding produces blank-dominated and temporally unstable segmentations that are difficult to correct manually. Our approach introduces two training-free blank-resolution strategies operating directly on CTC logits: (i) confidence-ratio substitution, which promotes competitive non-blank hypotheses relative to the blank symbol, and (ii) recursive context adjustment, which enforces local contextual consistency within blank spans. Experiments on English (TIMIT) and on Sardinian and Tyrolean dialect corpora show consistent improvements in boundary F1 prediction, phoneme duration regularity, and segmentation stability over greedy CTC decoding. Although absolute boundary deviations remain higher than transcript-conditioned aligners, the resulting alignments are structurally coherent and suitable for manual correction. A post-hoc phoneme-class analysis further reveals systematic asymmetries in blank resolution, highlighting complementary roles of local acoustic evidence and contextual cues, and outlining prominising venues for future improvements.
acl:2026.speakable-1.19.journal_ref: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026
acl:2026.speakable-1.19.title: Blank-Aware Decoding for Transcript-Free Phoneme Alignment in Low-Resource Languages and Dialects
acl:2026.speakable-1.19.venue: Proceedings of Speech Language Models in Low-Resource Settings: Performance, Evaluation, and Bias Analysis (SPEAKABLE) @ LREC 2026

acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.abstract: Social biases based on regional identity (or regional bias) are often observed in Indian contexts on major online social networks and require critical attention. However, due to large linguistic and cultural diversity, high annotation costs, and inherent human biases, very little annotated data exists on regional biases in the Indian context. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have garnered attention for the automatic annotation of text. However, such annotation efforts are largely limited to English texts, and LLMs often perform poorly when applied to low-resource languages. Therefore, this paper focuses on understanding the capabilities and challenges of popular open-source LLMs in annotating Indian regional biases. We utilize the recently proposed IndRegBias dataset, which consists of Indian regionally biased social media comments in both English and code-mixed formats. First, we assess the annotation capabilities of LLMs in a zero-shot setting and critically analyze their performance across different writing styles, including code-mixing, transliteration, and English. We find that the majority of LLMs exhibit low agreement with human annotations (measured using Cohen’s kappa). Consequently, we extend our study by fine-tuning the models using 50% of the data and evaluating them on the remaining 50%. We observe a significant improvement in annotation agreement (kappa) for all the LLMs. To further assess the capabilities of the fine-tuned models, we evaluate them on 500 newly collected social media comments discussing regional issues in India. The results show that most fine-tuned LLMs outperform their zero-shot counterparts when annotating these new comments.
acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)
acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.title: Annotating Indian Regional Biases using Large Language Models: Evaluation and Analysis
acl:2026.starsem-conference.16.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)

acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.abstract: Text detoxification, the automated detection and mitigation of abusive and harmful content, is essential for ensuring the safety of online communities and protecting users. However, low resource languages such as Tatar have received little research attention. In this paper we present Tatoxa, a novel state-of-the-art system for text detoxification in the Tatar language. Comparative experiments show that the proposed approach outperforms existing open source and proprietary commercial LLMs on key quality metrics. We also introduce a new dataset for text detoxification in Tatar, designed for fine tuning and evaluation in low resource settings. Finally, cross lingual transfer experiments indicate that transfer from other languages, including the culturally close Russian, performs significantly worse than training on native Tatar data even when a large Russian corpus is available.
acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)
acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.title: The Tatoxa System for Text Detoxification in Low-Resource Languages: The Case of Tatar
acl:2026.starsem-conference.17.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)

acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.abstract: A large body of research has examined the linguistic abilities of language models (LMs) across various languages. However, conclusive evidence regarding their semantic competence and world knowledge remains limited, especially for low-resource languages. In this study, we explore the semantic competence of Italian BabyLMs, focusing on their sensitivity to semantic violations. To this end, we adapt a minimal pair benchmark targeting semantic violations to evaluate the semantic abilities of BAMBI, a family of small-scale models trained on progressively larger and more complex datasets. We further compare their performance, assessed through accuracy, mean log-likelihood offset, and expected calibration error, with that of three larger Italian LMs. Our findings shed light on this aspect of semantic competence in small-scale models and how this is affected by data scale and training strategies.
acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)
acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.title: Can a Remedy Find a Researcher? Exploring the Development of Semantic Knowledge in Italian BabyLMs
acl:2026.starsem-conference.24.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Joint Conference on Lexical and Computational Semantics (*SEM 2026)

acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perpetuate cultural stereotypes not only through biased associations but through systematic omission and orthographic erasure of underrepresented languages. We present empirical evidence of two compounding failure modes affecting Northeast Indian languages: (1) entity-level invisibility, where state-of-the-art NER systems score F1=0.000 on culturally critical named entities such as Khasi surnames, Garo festivals, and tribal names; and (2) orthographic corruption, where LLM tokenizers corrupt semantically meaningful diacritics (ï, ñ) and the Garo morpheme boundary marker (U+00B7) at rates of 18.8–50% across four of five evaluated models. Drawing on NortheastNER (F1=0.964, six entity categories, XLM-RoBERTa-base) and a systematic tokenization study across Khasi and Garo, we argue that stereotype-by-omission constitutes a distinct and measurable harm to indigenous language communities. We further show that a custom multilingual tokenizer achieves 26–50% token reduction over five baseline LLMs, demonstrating that culturally grounded infrastructure can partially remediate these failures. Our findings call for cultural representation audits as a standard component of multilingual NLP evaluation.
acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Stereotypes Across Cultures in Language Technologies (StereACuLT 2026)
acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.title: Stereotyped by Silence: How LLMs Erase Northeast Indian Languages Through Omission and Orthographic Corruption
acl:2026.stereacult-1.6.venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Stereotypes Across Cultures in Language Technologies (StereACuLT 2026)

acl:2026.tacl-1.10.abstract: We introduce MultiBLiMP 1.0, a massively multilingual benchmark of linguistic minimal pairs, covering 101 languages and 2 types of subject-verb agreement, containing more than 128,000 minimal pairs. Our minimal pairs are created using a fully automated pipeline, leveraging the large-scale linguistic resources of Universal Dependencies and UniMorph. MultiBLiMP 1.0 evaluates abilities of LLMs at an unprecedented multilingual scale, and highlights the shortcomings of the current state-of-the-art in modelling low-resource languages.1
acl:2026.tacl-1.10.journal_ref: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

glossary.explanation_id: Pasangan kalimat yang hampir identik yang hanya berbeda dalam satu aspek spesifik untuk menguji pelanggaran gramatikal.
Sebuah koleksi *treebank* multibahasa yang menyediakan anotasi sintaksis dan morfologis yang seragam.
Koleksi multibahasa dari anotasi fitur morfologis yang mendefinisikan fitur tingkat kata untuk berbagai bahasa.
Sebuah ukuran seberapa baik model probabilitas memprediksi sampel data.
Analisis struktur gramatikal kalimat yang merepresentasikan hubungan antarkata dalam bentuk dependensi.
Tahap pelatihan lanjutan pada *large language model* setelah tahap *pre-training* dasar selesai.

background.en: Large language models are often trained on multilingual corpora and evaluated extensively on functional linguistic competence through tasks requiring world knowledge and understanding. However, little work has assessed their formal linguistic competence, which refers to the knowledge of rules and statistical regularities of a language. Existing targeted syntactic evaluation benchmarks structured as minimal pairs are largely limited to English and a few high-resource languages.
background.id: *Large language model* sering dilatih pada korpus multibahasa dan dievaluasi secara ekstensif pada kompetensi linguistik fungsional melalui tugas-tugas yang memerlukan pengetahuan dan pemahaman dunia. Namun, sedikit pekerjaan yang menilai kompetensi linguistik formal mereka, yang mengacu pada pengetahuan tentang aturan dan keteraturan statistik dari suatu bahasa. *Benchmark* evaluasi sintaksis terarah yang ada dan terstruktur sebagai *minimal pair* sebagian besar terbatas pada bahasa Inggris dan beberapa bahasa *high-resource*.

contributions.en: The paper introduces MultiBLiMP 1.0, a massively multilingual benchmark containing more than 128,000 minimal pairs across 101 languages. The authors propose a fully automated pipeline leveraging Universal Dependencies and UniMorph to extract candidates, validate agreement conditions using collocation statistics, and perform inflection and dataset balancing. Additionally, they provide a comprehensive evaluation of 42 large language models.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan MultiBLiMP 1.0, sebuah *benchmark* multibahasa massal yang berisi lebih dari 128.000 *minimal pair* di 101 bahasa. Para penulis mengusulkan *pipeline* otomatis yang memanfaatkan Universal Dependencies dan UniMorph untuk mengekstrak kandidat, memvalidasi kondisi persetujuan menggunakan statistik kolokasi, serta melakukan infleksi dan penyeimbangan data. Selain itu, mereka menyajikan evaluasi komprehensif terhadap 42 *large language model*.

future_work.en: The authors state limitations regarding the reliance on the size, diversity, and annotation quality of Universal Dependencies and UniMorph, as well as the challenge of extending the procedure to more complex phenomena. Future work includes expanding MultiBLiMP to more constructions beyond subject-verb agreement and enabling quantitative typological studies.
future_work.id: Para penulis menyatakan keterbatasan terkait ketergantungan pada ukuran, keragaman, dan kualitas anotasi dari Universal Dependencies dan UniMorph, serta tantangan dalam memperluas prosedur ke fenomena yang lebih kompleks. Pekerjaan masa depan mencakup memperluas MultiBLiMP ke lebih banyak konstruksi di luar persetujuan subjek-verba dan memungkinkan studi tipologis kuantitatif.

method.en: The automated pipeline consists of four stages: candidate extraction using dependency parse trees, agreement validation based on Universal Dependencies and UniMorph collocation statistics, word inflection to create ungrammatical counterparts, and weighted downsampling to balance morphological features and sentence-level characteristics. The authors evaluate 42 large language models, including base and chat versions, using accuracy and log probability difference metrics.
method.id: *Pipeline* otomatis terdiri dari empat tahap: ekstraksi kandidat menggunakan pohon *parse* dependensi, validasi persetujuan berdasarkan statistik kolokasi Universal Dependencies dan UniMorph, infleksi kata untuk membuat padanan yang tidak gramatikal, serta *downsampling* terbobot untuk menyeimbangkan fitur morfologis dan karakteristik tingkat kalimat. Para penulis mengevaluasi 42 *large language model*, termasuk versi *base* dan *chat*, menggunakan metrik akurasi dan perbedaan probabilitas log.

related_work.en: Previous targeted syntactic evaluation began with English subject-verb number agreement using minimal pairs extracted from Wikipedia, which was later extended using context-free grammars and template-based generation in BLiMP. While monolingual non-English benchmarks have recently been developed for languages such as Chinese, Japanese, Dutch, and Swahili, existing multilingual minimal pair benchmarks like CLAMS only cover five languages.
related_work.id: Evaluasi sintaksis terarah sebelumnya dimulai dengan persetujuan nomor subjek-verba bahasa Inggris menggunakan *minimal pair* yang diekstrak dari Wikipedia, yang kemudian diperluas menggunakan tata bahasa *context-free* dan pembuatan berbasis templat di BLiMP. Meskipun *benchmark* ekstensif non-Inggris monolingual baru-baru ini dikembangkan untuk bahasa seperti Mandarin, Jepang, Belanda, dan Swahili, *benchmark* *minimal pair* multibahasa yang ada seperti CLAMS hanya mencakup lima bahasa.

results.en: Evaluation results show that linguistic competence is strongly driven by model size and language frequency in the training data, and can deteriorate as a result of post-training. Llama3-70B-base and Gemma3-27B-base achieve the highest overall average accuracy at 90.2 percent. Furthermore, cross-model comparisons indicate that language-specific pre-training has a stronger effect on linguistic ability than post-training.
results.id: Hasil evaluasi menunjukkan bahwa kompetensi linguistik sangat didorong oleh ukuran model dan frekuensi bahasa dalam data pelatihan, serta dapat memburuk sebagai hasil dari *post-training*. Llama3-70B-base dan Gemma3-27B-base mencapai akurasi rata-rata keseluruhan tertinggi sebesar 90,2 persen. Lebih lanjut, perbandingan antar model menunjukkan bahwa *pre-training* khusus bahasa memiliki efek yang lebih kuat pada kemampuan linguistik daripada *post-training*.

tldr.en: We introduce MultiBLiMP 1.0, a massively multilingual benchmark of linguistic minimal pairs covering 101 languages and two types of subject-verb agreement. Our evaluation of 42 large language models highlights significant shortcomings in modelling low-resource languages.
tldr.id: Kami memperkenalkan MultiBLiMP 1.0, sebuah *benchmark* *minimal pair* linguistik yang sangat multibahasa mencakup 101 bahasa dan dua jenis persetujuan subjek-verba. Evaluasi kami terhadap 42 *large language model* menyoroti kelemahan signifikan dalam pemodelan bahasa *low-resource*.

acl:2026.tacl-1.10.title: MultiBLiMP 1.0: A Massively Multilingual Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs
acl:2026.tacl-1.10.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

acl:2026.tacl-1.17.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) with limited data poses a practical challenge in low-resource languages, specialized domains, and constrained deployment settings. While pre-trained LLMs provide strong foundations, effective adaptation under data scarcity requires focused and efficient fine-tuning techniques. This paper presents a structured and practical survey of recent methods for fine-tuning LLMs in data-scarce scenarios. We systematically review parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques that lower training and deployment costs, domain and cross-lingual adaptation methods for both encoder and decoder models, and model specialization strategies. We further examine preference alignment approaches that guide model behavior using limited human or synthetic feedback, emphasizing sample and compute efficiency. Throughout, we highlight empirical trade-offs, selection criteria, and best practices for choosing suitable techniques based on task constraints, including model scaling, data scaling, and the mitigation of catastrophic forgetting. The aim is to equip researchers and practitioners with actionable insights for effectively fine-tuning LLMs when data and resources are limited.
acl:2026.tacl-1.17.journal_ref: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

glossary.explanation_id: Pendekatan *fine-tuning* *model bahasa* yang hanya memperbarui sebagian kecil parameter untuk menghemat biaya komputasi.
Fenomena hilangnya kemampuan atau pengetahuan lama pada *model* ketika *model* tersebut mempelajari tugas atau *domain* baru.
Proses penyesuaian perilaku *model* agar selaras dengan preferensi manusia atau nilai-nilai tertentu.
Tahap pelatihan lanjutan pada *model bahasa* pra-latihan menggunakan *korpus* tak terawasi untuk beradaptasi dengan *domain* atau bahasa tertentu.
Teknik *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang mendekati pembaruan bobot *model* menggunakan matriks berperingkat rendah.
Proses pelatihan *model* menggunakan data beranotasi untuk mengikuti instruksi atau menyelesaikan tugas tertentu.
Teknik menggabungkan beberapa *model* yang dilatih dengan konfigurasi berbeda langsung di ruang bobot tanpa pelatihan tambahan.
Metode pembelajaran yang mendekatkan representasi data yang serupa dan menjauhkan data yang tidak serupa.

background.en: Fine-tuning large language models with limited data is a persistent challenge in low-resource languages, specialized domains, and constrained deployment settings. While pre-trained models provide strong foundations, naive adaptation under data scarcity risks overfitting, catastrophic forgetting, and poor generalization. A structured and pragmatic review is necessary to navigate current strategies and make informed choices under real-world resource constraints.
background.id: Pelaksanaan *fine-tuning* *large language model* dengan data terbatas merupakan tantangan nyata dalam bahasa ber-*resource* rendah, *domain* khusus, dan pengoperasian yang terbatas. Meskipun *model bahasa* pra-latihan memberikan fondasi yang kuat, adaptasi naif di tengah kelangkaan data berisiko menimbulkan *overfitting*, *catastrophic forgetting*, dan generalisasi yang buruk. Ulasan yang terstruktur dan pragmatis sangat diperlukan untuk menavigasi strategi saat ini dan membuat pilihan yang tepat di bawah batasan sumber daya dunia nyata.

contributions.en: The paper provides a structured survey and practical guide across four main areas: parameter-efficient fine-tuning, domain and cross-lingual adaptation, model specialization strategies, and preference alignment approaches. It highlights empirical trade-offs, selection criteria, and best practices regarding model scaling, data scaling, and mitigating catastrophic forgetting, equipping researchers with actionable insights.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyajikan ulasan terstruktur dan panduan praktis yang mencakup empat area utama: *parameter-efficient fine-tuning*, adaptasi *domain* dan lintas-bahasa, strategi spesialisasi *model*, dan pendekatan *preference alignment*. Makalah ini menyoroti *trade-off* empiris, kriteria pemilihan, dan praktik terbaik terkait *scaling* *model*, *scaling* data, serta mitigasi *catastrophic forgetting*, guna membekali para peneliti dengan wawasan yang dapat diterapkan secara langsung.

future_work.en: The authors highlight that the effects of alignment strategies on downstream outcomes remain underexplored, particularly regarding model scale, output style, and non-English settings. They also note that the nonlinear interactions underlying model merging are poorly understood, motivating further research into transparent reporting, evaluation metrics, and non-English domain applications.
future_work.id: Penulis menyoroti bahwa efek strategi *alignment* terhadap kinerja hilir masih kurang dieksplorasi, terutama dalam kaitannya dengan skala *model*, gaya keluaran, dan pengaturan non-Inggris. Mereka juga mencatat bahwa interaksi nonlinier yang mendasari *model merging* belum dipahami dengan baik, sehingga memotivasi penelitian lebih lanjut mengenai pelaporan transparan, *metrik* evaluasi, dan penerapan pada *domain* non-Inggris.

method.en: The authors systematically review literature across the post-pretraining pipeline. For parameter-efficient fine-tuning, methods are organized into parameter composition, input composition, function composition, and hybrid methods. For domain and cross-lingual adaptation, they examine continued pre-training, encoder-decoder strategies, contrastive and adversarial learning, and limited supervision. For preference alignment, they analyze reinforcement learning methods, direct preference optimization, reference-free approaches, and alignment during supervised fine-tuning.
method.id: Penulis meninjau literatur secara sistematis di sepanjang *pipeline* pasca-pra-latihan. Untuk *parameter-efficient fine-tuning*, metode dikelompokkan ke dalam komposisi parameter, komposisi input, komposisi fungsi, dan metode hibrida. Untuk adaptasi *domain* dan lintas-bahasa, penulis meneliti *continued pre-training*, strategi *encoder-decoder*, *contrastive learning* dan *adversarial learning*, serta supervisi terbatas. Untuk *preference alignment*, mereka menganalisis metode *reinforcement learning*, *direct preference optimization*, pendekatan bebas referensi, serta *alignment* selama *supervised fine-tuning*.

related_work.en: Several prior surveys address isolated aspects such as data augmentation, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, efficient training techniques, low-resource supervised NLP, instruction tuning, or preference alignment. However, these works typically focus on specific segments of model development. In contrast, this paper offers an integrated survey of the full post-pretraining pipeline, emphasizing practical insights, comparative trade-offs, and methodological guidance for data-scarce scenarios.
related_work.id: Beberapa ulasan sebelumnya membahas aspek-aspek terisolasi seperti augmentasi data, *parameter-efficient fine-tuning*, teknik pelatihan efisien, NLP terawasi *low-resource*, *instruction tuning*, atau *preference alignment*. Namun, karya-karya tersebut umumnya berfokus pada segmen tertentu dari pengembangan *model*. Sebaliknya, makalah ini menawarkan ulasan terintegrasi mengenai *pipeline* pasca-pra-latihan secara utuh, dengan menekankan wawasan praktis, komparasi *trade-off*, dan panduan metodologis untuk skenario kekurangan data.

results.en: Key findings show that parameter-efficient fine-tuning often matches or outperforms full fine-tuning under 100k samples, while full fine-tuning becomes favorable with million-scale datasets. Data quality frequently outweighs quantity, and a small number of diverse, high-quality examples can surpass larger noisy datasets. Furthermore, model size has a larger impact than fine-tuning or pre-training data size, and larger models consistently demonstrate better sample efficiency.
results.id: Temuan utama menunjukkan bahwa *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* sering kali menyaingi atau melampaui *full fine-tuning* di bawah 100.000 sampel, sementara *full fine-tuning* menjadi lebih unggul pada *dataset* berskala jutaan. Kualitas data sering kali lebih menentukan daripada kuantitas, di mana sejumlah kecil contoh yang beragam dan berkualitas tinggi dapat mengungguli *dataset* besar yang bising. Selain itu, ukuran *model* berdampak lebih besar daripada ukuran data *fine-tuning* atau pra-latihan, dan *model* yang lebih besar secara konsisten menunjukkan efisiensi sampel yang lebih baik.

tldr.en: This paper presents a structured survey of recent methods for fine-tuning large language models in data-scarce scenarios. It provides actionable insights and best practices for parameter-efficient adaptation, domain specialization, and preference alignment under limited data and resources.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan tinjauan terstruktur mengenai metode terkini untuk *fine-tuning* *large language model* dalam skenario keterbatasan data. Penelitian ini memberikan wawasan praktis dan praktik terbaik untuk adaptasi *parameter-efficient*, spesialisasi *domain*, dan *preference alignment* di bawah keterbatasan data dan sumber daya.

acl:2026.tacl-1.17.title: Fine-tuning Large Language Models with Limited Data: A Survey and Practical Guide
acl:2026.tacl-1.17.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

acl:2026.tacl-1.19.abstract: This paper introduces MERLIN, a novel testbed system for the task of Multilingual Multimodal Entity Linking. The created dataset includes BBC news article titles, paired with corresponding images, in five languages: Hindi, Japanese, Indonesian, Vietnamese, and Tamil, featuring over 7,000 named entity mentions linked to 2,500 unique Wikidata entities. We also include several benchmarks using multilingual and multimodal entity linking methods exploring different language models like LLaMa-2 and Aya-23. Our findings indicate that incorporating visual data improves the accuracy of entity linking, especially for entities where the textual context is ambiguous or insufficient, and particularly for models that do not have strong multilingual abilities. For the work, the dataset, methods are available online.1
acl:2026.tacl-1.19.journal_ref: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

glossary.explanation_id: *Entity linking* adalah tugas menghubungkan penyebutan entitas dalam teks ke entitas yang sesuai di dalam *knowledge base*.
Pendekatan *multimodal* melibatkan pemrosesan dan penggabungan lebih dari satu jenis data atau modalitas, seperti teks dan gambar.
Pembelajaran *zero-shot* adalah kemampuan model untuk melakukan tugas baru tanpa pelatihan atau contoh spesifik sebelumnya pada tugas tersebut.
*Knowledge base* adalah basis data terstruktur yang menyimpan informasi, fakta, dan hubungan antar entitas di dunia.
Disambiguasi adalah proses menyelesaikan keambiguan ketika satu kata atau penyebutan dapat merujuk pada beberapa entitas yang berbeda.
*Recall@1* adalah metrik evaluasi yang mengukur apakah entitas yang benar berada di peringkat teratas dari prediksi model.
*Autoregressive* adalah metode pembuatan teks atau keluaran di mana model menghasilkan token satu per satu secara berurutan.

background.en: Entity linking involves mapping ambiguous entity mentions from unstructured text to unambiguous referents in a knowledge base. While traditional entity linking focuses solely on text, short or context-dependent statements often lack sufficient information for disambiguation, a problem exacerbated in non-English low-resource languages. Incorporating visual modalities alongside multilingual text presents a promising direction to resolve these ambiguities, yet a comprehensive benchmark combining multilinguality and multimodality has been absent.
background.id: *Entity linking* melibatkan pemetaan penyebutan entitas yang ambigu dari teks tak terstruktur ke referen yang tidak ambigu dalam sebuah *knowledge base*. Meskipun *entity linking* tradisional berfokus semata-mata pada teks, pernyataan yang pendek atau bergantung pada konteks seringkali kekurangan informasi yang cukup untuk disambiguasi, sebuah masalah yang diperparah pada bahasa *low-resource* non-Inggris. Penggabungan modalitas visual bersama teks multibahasa menghadirkan arah yang menjanjikan untuk mengatasi ambiguitas tersebut, namun *benchmark* komprehensif yang menggabungkan multibahasa dan multimodal belum tersedia sebelumnya.

contributions.en: The paper introduces MERLIN, the first testbed and dataset for multilingual multimodal entity linking, featuring over 7,000 named entity mentions linked to 2,500 unique Wikidata entities across five diverse languages: Hindi, Japanese, Indonesian, Vietnamese, and Tamil. It provides robust benchmarks using state-of-the-art models like mGENRE, GEMEL-Llama-2, and GEMEL-Aya-23, and demonstrates through rigorous analysis how visual context aids entity disambiguation especially when textual data is insufficient.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *MERLIN*, *testbed* dan dataset pertama untuk *multilingual multimodal entity linking*, yang menampilkan lebih dari 7.000 sebutan entitas bernama yang tertaut ke 2.500 entitas Wikidata unik di lima bahasa yang beragam: Hindi, Jepang, Indonesia, Vietnam, dan Tamil. Makalah ini menyediakan *benchmark* yang kokoh menggunakan model mutakhir seperti mGENRE, GEMEL-Llama-2, dan GEMEL-Aya-23, serta mendemonstrasikan melalui analisis ketat bagaimana konteks visual membantu disambiguasi entitas terutama ketika data teks tidak mencukupi.

future_work.en: The authors note limitations including the exclusive reliance on BBC news articles which restricts genre diversity, potential human annotation inconsistencies, and the use of Wikipedia page titles instead of direct Wikidata QIDs in baselines. Future work should explore expanding datasets to diverse text domains, refining models to better handle entity ambiguity in lower-resourced languages, and implementing direct Wikidata QID linking strategies.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat keterbatasan termasuk ketergantungan eksklusif pada artikel berita BBC yang membatasi keragaman genre, potensi inkonsistensi anotasi manusia, dan penggunaan judul halaman Wikipedia alih-alih QID Wikidata langsung pada *baseline*. Penelitian mendatang harus mengeksplorasi perluasan dataset ke domain teks yang beragam, menyempurnakan model untuk menangani ambiguitas entitas dengan lebih baik pada bahasa *low-resource*, dan menerapkan strategi penautan QID Wikidata langsung.

method.en: The authors curated MERLIN by selecting 1,000 BBC news article titles per language from the M3LS dataset, pairing them with corresponding images, and performing rigorous crowdsourced annotation via INCEpTION with strict pre-screening and majority voting. For evaluation, they benchmarked unimodal text-based mGENRE alongside multimodal generative models GEMEL-Llama-2 and GEMEL-Aya-23, utilizing a frozen vision encoder and LLM while training a feature mapper for cross-modal interactions in a zero-shot setting.
method.id: Para penulis mengkurasi *MERLIN* dengan memilih 1.000 judul artikel berita BBC per bahasa dari dataset M3LS, memasangkannya dengan gambar yang sesuai, dan melakukan anotasi *crowdsourced* yang ketat melalui INCEpTION dengan *pre-screening* ketat dan *majority voting*. Untuk evaluasi, mereka menguji mGENRE berbasis teks unimodal berdampingan dengan model generatif multimodal GEMEL-Llama-2 dan GEMEL-Aya-23, menggunakan *vision encoder* dan *large language model* yang dibekukan sambil melatih *feature mapper* untuk interaksi lintas modal dalam pengaturan *zero-shot*.

related_work.en: Prior research in entity linking has predominantly addressed text-based and monolingual settings, or explored cross-lingual approaches linking one language to English knowledge bases. Although recent advancements introduced massively multilingual models and multimodal entity linking datasets for English such as Twitter and WikiDiverse, they failed to bridge multilinguality and multimodality simultaneously. Furthermore, traditional two-stage pipeline approaches suffer from compounded errors, prompting the adoption of generative and autoregressive entity linking methods.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya dalam *entity linking* sebagian besar membahas pengaturan berbasis teks dan ekabahasa, atau mengeksplorasi pendekatan lintas bahasa yang menghubungkan satu bahasa ke *knowledge base* berbahasa Inggris. Meskipun kemajuan baru-baru ini memperkenalkan model multibahasa masif dan dataset *multimodal entity linking* untuk bahasa Inggris seperti Twitter dan WikiDiverse, mereka gagal menjembatani multibahasa dan multimodal secara bersamaan. Selain itu, pendekatan *pipeline* dua tahap tradisional mengalami penumpukan galat, yang mendorong adopsi metode *generative* dan *autoregressive entity linking*.

results.en: Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating visual context consistently improves Recall@1 accuracy across languages, particularly for models like Llama-2 that lack strong native multilingual abilities. Specifically, mGENRE achieves high performance in Indonesian with an R@1 of 78.93%, while GEMEL-Aya-23 reaches 75.00% with visual inputs. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations reveal that visual cues are exceptionally beneficial for resolving ambiguous mentions and person entities, though models still struggle significantly with low-resource languages such as Tamil.
results.id: Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa penggabungan konteks visual secara konsisten meningkatkan akurasi *Recall@1* di berbagai bahasa, terutama untuk model seperti Llama-2 yang tidak memiliki kemampuan multibahasa bawaan yang kuat. Secara khusus, mGENRE mencapai performa tinggi di bahasa Indonesia dengan R@1 sebesar 78.93%, sementara GEMEL-Aya-23 mencapai 75.00% dengan masukan visual. Evaluasi kualitatif dan kuantitatif mengungkapkan bahwa petunjuk visual sangat bermanfaat untuk mengurai sebutan yang ambigu dan entitas orang, meskipun model masih mengalami kesulitan yang signifikan dengan bahasa *low-resource* seperti bahasa Tamil.

tldr.en: This paper introduces MERLIN, a novel testbed for multilingual multimodal entity linking across five languages using news articles and images. The findings show that incorporating visual data improves entity linking accuracy, particularly for ambiguous contexts and models with limited multilingual capabilities.
tldr.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan *MERLIN*, sebuah *testbed* baru untuk *multilingual multimodal entity linking* di lima bahasa menggunakan artikel berita dan gambar. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggabungan data visual meningkatkan akurasi *entity linking*, terutama untuk konteks yang ambigu dan model dengan kemampuan multibahasa yang terbatas.

acl:2026.tacl-1.19.title: MERLIN: A Testbed for Multilingual Multimodal Entity Recognition and Linking
acl:2026.tacl-1.19.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

acl:2026.tacl-1.56.abstract: Understanding culture requires reasoning across context, tradition, and implicit social knowledge, far beyond recalling isolated facts. Yet most culturally focused question answering (QA) benchmarks rely on singlehop questions, which may allow models to exploit shallow cues rather than demonstrate genuine cultural reasoning. In this work, we introduce ID-MoCQA, the first large-scale multi-hop QA dataset for assessing the cultural understanding of large language models (LLMs), grounded in Indonesian traditions and available in both English and Indonesian. We present a new framework that systematically transforms single-hop cultural questions into multi-hop reasoning chains spanning six clue types (e.g., commonsense, temporal, geographical). Our multi-stage validation pipeline, combining expert review and LLM-as-a-judge filtering, ensures high-quality question-answer pairs. Our evaluation across state-of-the-art models reveals substantial gaps in cultural reasoning, particularly in tasks requiring nuanced inference. ID-MoCQA provides a challenging and essential benchmark for advancing the cultural competency of LLMs.1
acl:2026.tacl-1.56.journal_ref: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14
acl:2026.tacl-1.56.title: No Shortcuts to Culture: Indonesian Multi-hop Question Answering for Complex Cultural Understanding
acl:2026.tacl-1.56.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Volume 14

acl:2026.udw-1.2.abstract: This study uses Universal Dependencies to investigate subject omission across fifty-six news corpora and twenty geographic varieties of English. Building on McLuhan’s "hot–cool" distinction, Hall’s LC–HC continuum, and Bisang’s notion of overt vs. hidden complexity, it tests whether subject omission rates reflect degrees of contextual reliance. The results broadly support these theories: low-context, "hot" languages, such as German, Dutch and Swedish, show low omission rates, while high-context, "cool" languages, such as Japanese, Korean and Chinese, show higher rates. English behaves as a "hot" language but exhibits internal variation across varieties, with Southeast Asian varieties exhibiting more omission than African ones. The study provides large-scale quantitative evidence while highlighting the need for further theoretical and methodological refinement, particularly regarding the role of word order and agreement.
acl:2026.udw-1.2.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on Universal Dependencies (UDW 2026)
acl:2026.udw-1.2.title: Which languages are "hot", and which are "cool"? Using Universal Dependencies for large-scale comparisons of subject expression
acl:2026.udw-1.2.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on Universal Dependencies (UDW 2026)

acl:2026.udw-1.21.abstract: This paper introduces the first steps towards the creation of a novel resource for contemporary Sardinian within the Universal Dependencies framework. Sardinian is a Romance language spoken in Sardinia, an island belonging to the Italian Republic and located in the center of the western Mediterranean. It is a minority and endangered language, traditionally transmitted mainly orally, and characterized by a multiplicity of varieties (usually grouped into two macro-varieties Logudorese and Campidanese), all recognized as part of the Sardinian linguistic continuum. These varieties share basic morphosyntactic features, while presenting differences at the lexical level and in the realization of specific constructions. This internal variation can be particularly challenging with regard to the normalization of lemmas and the linguistic characterization of certain phenomena. The development of the treebank therefore aims to provide an annotated resource for contemporary Sardinian that takes into account the specificities of the different varieties, using Universal Dependencies to represent them within a unified theoretical framework, in order to facilitate both linguistic analysis and automatic processing. The present paper thus describes some linguistic characteristics of Sardinian and the attempts to encode them within the UD framework. Finally, we present the results of our evaluation of an NLP pipeline for Sardinian, trained on our corpus, for the Stanford Stanza parser.
acl:2026.udw-1.21.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on Universal Dependencies (UDW 2026)
acl:2026.udw-1.21.title: Introducing Universal Dependencies for Sardinian: the UD ContSar Treebank
acl:2026.udw-1.21.venue: Proceedings of the Ninth Workshop on Universal Dependencies (UDW 2026)

acl:2026.unlp-1.14.abstract: Adapting large language models to low-resource languages presents three interconnected challenges: inefficient tokenization, scarcity of high-quality annotated data, and limited resources for instruction tuning. We present a reproducible approach that addresses each challenge using data-centric methods that primarily rely on unlabeled text corpora, parallel translation data, and a multilingual base model. Our approach combines (1) vocabulary surgery for tokenizer adaptation without full retraining, (2) cross-lingual transfer of quality classifiers via translation, enabling filtering without target-language annotations, and (3) generation of instruction data through translation, task conversion, and targeted synthesis. We validate this recipe by adapting Gemma-3-12B to Ukrainian. %, producing Lapa-12BOur pretrained model achieves top performance on Ukrainian benchmarks, while our instruction-tuned variant demonstrates strong performance on translation (33 BLEU on FLORES), summarization, and question-answering tasks, while requiring 1.5x fewer tokens than the original model for the same text. We release all models, datasets, classifiers, and code to enable replication for other languages.
acl:2026.unlp-1.14.journal_ref: Proceedings of the Fifth Ukrainian Natural Language Processing Conference (UNLP 2026)
acl:2026.unlp-1.14.title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of Multilingual LLMs to Ukrainian
acl:2026.unlp-1.14.venue: Proceedings of the Fifth Ukrainian Natural Language Processing Conference (UNLP 2026)

acl:2026.wildre-1.14.abstract: Language identification (LID) is crucial for natural language processing systems, yet Northeast Indian languages remain severely underserved by existing multilingual LID models. We present NE-LID, a fast and accurate language identification system specifically designed for eleven languages of Northeast India. Built using character n-gram features with fastText, NE-LID achieves 99.09% accuracy on a balanced test set, significantly outperforming existing multilingual systems including GlotLID (73.12%), OpenLID (42.03%), IndicLID (39.30%), and LangDetect (24.33%). Our model processes predictions in 0.084 milliseconds on average, enabling real-time applications. We demonstrate that character-level modeling outperforms transformer-based approaches for script-diverse, low-resource languages
acl:2026.wildre-1.14.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 8th Workshop on Indian Language Data: Resources and Evaluation
acl:2026.wildre-1.14.title: NE-LID: A Fast and Accurate Language Identification System for Northeast Indian Languages
acl:2026.wildre-1.14.venue: Proceedings of the 8th Workshop on Indian Language Data: Resources and Evaluation

acl:2026.wildre-1.3.abstract: Indian languages are deeply embedded in cultural traditions, oral narratives, regional lexicons, and socially grounded communicative practices. However, existing speech resources and large multilingual ASR models often underrepresent culturally rich and naturally occurring speech varieties. In this paper, we introduce Konkani Daan, a community-driven initiative for collecting culturally grounded speech data for the Konkani language. The corpus currently comprises over 43.9 hours of 16 kHz speech recordings contributed through a web-based participatory platform. We evaluate a strong multilingual baseline, AI4Bharat IndicConformer-600M, in zero-shot mode on the Konkani Daan development set (379 utterances), achieving Word Error Rate (WER) of 46.46% and Character Error Rate (CER) of 15.47%, indicating substantial domain and cultural mismatch. Through qualitative error analysis, we identify systematic challenges including compound word segmentation, numeric normalisation, named entity distortion, and orthographic variation. Our findings demonstrate that culturally dense community speech exposes systematic limitations in multilingual ASR systems and motivates normalisation-aware and culturally informed evaluation strategies.
acl:2026.wildre-1.3.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 8th Workshop on Indian Language Data: Resources and Evaluation
acl:2026.wildre-1.3.title: Konkani Daan: A Community-Driven Culturally Grounded Speech Corpus for Low-Resource ASR
acl:2026.wildre-1.3.venue: Proceedings of the 8th Workshop on Indian Language Data: Resources and Evaluation

acl:2026.wildre-1.4.abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) has been a core task of natural language processing (NLP) since the Message Understanding Conferences (MUCs). Data annotation plays a crucial role in this task. However, existing annotation studies often rely on the literal sense of entities. Such annotations may lead to inconsistencies, while resolving ambiguity introduced by figurative tropes like metonymy. For example, in India won the series, India refers to a sports team instead of a geographic location. Understanding such non-literal senses is crucial for various NLP applications such as Question Answering, Information Extraction, etc. By addressing this gap, this study presents an annotation framework and detailed guidelines for annotating metonymic readings of named entities in Marathi, an Indo-Aryan language spoken in the central-western region of India. The study uses news corpus from various domains. It presents a two-tiered annotation framework for annotating conventional metonymies in Marathi language. Further, it describes the annotation framework applied to a corpus of 1,279 Marathi sentences. The result shows the inadequacy of literal-only annotation as 53.6% of named entity spans have metonymic readings. This study makes a crucial contribution for resource development for low-resource languages that share similar linguistic structures and cultural contexts. The paper describes the framework with necessary examples, challenges and concludes with a future scope.
acl:2026.wildre-1.4.journal_ref: Proceedings of the 8th Workshop on Indian Language Data: Resources and Evaluation
acl:2026.wildre-1.4.title: Is Literal Annotation Enough? Building an Annotation Framework for Metonymic Named Entities in Marathi
acl:2026.wildre-1.4.venue: Proceedings of the 8th Workshop on Indian Language Data: Resources and Evaluation

doi:10.1007/s00521-026-12339-x.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models are increasingly used for embedding extraction. In fact, there are many approaches that try to optimize the embedding representations that these models can learn, exploiting the knowledge gained from extensive pre-training and large parameter counts. However, most works currently focus on the English language and textual input only, reflecting the trend of current Large Language Model training corpora. Recently, several Large Vision-Language Models, which are Large Language Models capable of processing multimodal signals in input, have been released. Yet, their training procedure still remains predominantly based on English data. This limitation also affects the evaluation step, with embedding benchmarks that provide limited coverage for low-resource languages. To address these challenges, we adapt a Large Vision-Language Embedding Model trained on English multimodal tasks to support multilingual inputs. Furthermore, we introduce a new benchmark to evaluate the multilingual and multimodal capabilities of embedding models.
doi:10.1007/s00521-026-12339-x.title: MAMMa: adaptation of multimodal LLM embeddings to multilinguality

doi:10.1007/s00521-026-12361-z.title: Construction of anti-interference translation model for low-resource languages based on translation training

doi:10.1007/s10579-026-09951-7.abstract: Abstract Authorship analysis plays an important role in diverse domains, including forensic linguistics, academia, cybersecurity, and digital content authentication. This paper presents a systematic literature review on two key sub-tasks of authorship analysis; Authorship Attribution and Authorship Verification. The review explores SOTA methodologies, ranging from traditional ML approaches to DL models and LLMs, highlighting their evolution, strengths, and limitations, based on studies conducted from 2015 to 2024. Key contributions include a detailed analysis of methods, techniques, their corresponding feature extraction techniques, datasets used, and emerging challenges in authorship analysis. The study highlights critical research gaps, particularly in low-resource language processing, multilingual adaptation, cross-domain generalization, and AI-generated text detection. This review aims to help researchers by giving an overview of the latest trends and challenges in authorship analysis. It also points out possible areas for future study. The goal is to support the development of better, more reliable, and accurate authorship analysis system in diverse textual domain.

glossary.explanation_id: Tugas penentuan penulis dari suatu teks berdasarkan gaya penulisan.
Tugas untuk menentukan apakah dua teks ditulis oleh penulis yang sama atau berbeda.
Cabang ilmu bahasa yang diterapkan dalam bidang hukum dan investigasi kriminal.
Proses mengekstrak ciri atau karakteristik penting dari data mentah untuk digunakan dalam *model*.

background.en: Authorship analysis plays an important role in diverse domains, including forensic linguistics, academia, cybersecurity, and digital content authentication. Despite its significance, the field faces critical research gaps, particularly in low-resource language processing, multilingual adaptation, cross-domain generalization, and AI-generated text detection.
background.id: Analisis kepengarangan memegang peranan penting dalam berbagai domain, termasuk linguistik forensik, akademisi, keamanan siber, dan autentikasi konten digital. Terlepas dari signifikansinya, bidang ini menghadapi kesenjangan penelitian yang kritis, terutama dalam pemrosesan bahasa *low-resource*, adaptasi multibahasa, generalisasi lintas domain, dan deteksi teks buatan AI.

contributions.en: The key contributions of this paper include a detailed analysis of methods, techniques, and their corresponding feature extraction techniques. Additionally, the study examines datasets used, emerging challenges, and research gaps in authorship analysis to guide future research.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama dari makalah ini mencakup analisis mendetail mengenai metode, teknik, dan teknik ekstraksi fitur yang bersesuaian. Selain itu, studi ini mengkaji dataset yang digunakan, tantangan yang muncul, dan kesenjangan penelitian dalam analisis kepengarangan untuk memandu penelitian di masa depan.

future_work.en: The authors point out possible areas for future study, aiming to support the development of better, more reliable, and accurate authorship analysis systems across diverse textual domains.

doi:10.1007/s40747-026-02498-8.abstract: Due to the scarcity of part-of-speech (POS) annotated data for low-resource languages, existing studies have predominantly relied on unsupervised methods. Among these methods, annotation projection transfers POS tags from a high-resource source language to a low-resource target language through word alignments derived from parallel corpora, making it particularly suitable for low-resource scenarios. However, its effectiveness depends heavily on the availability of parallel corpora, which remain scarce or entirely unavailable for many low-resource languages. To address this limitation, we propose a fully unsupervised cross-lingual POS tagging framework that relies solely on monolingual corpora and leverages an unsupervised neural machine translation (UNMT) system. Specifically, the UNMT system translates sentences from a high-resource language into a low-resource language to construct pseudo-parallel sentence pairs. A target language POS tagger is then trained based on the standard annotation projection procedure. Moreover, we introduce a multi-source projection technique to calibrate the POS tags projected on the target side, thereby improving the quality of the annotations used to train the target language POS tagger. We evaluate the proposed framework on 28 language pairs, covering four source languages (English, German, Spanish and French) and seven target languages (Afrikaans, Basque, Finnish, Indonesian, Lithuanian, Portuguese and Turkish). Experimental results show that our method achieves performance comparable to that of a baseline cross-lingual POS tagger trained on genuine parallel sentence pairs and even outperforms it for several target languages. Furthermore, the proposed multi-source projection technique further improves tagging performance, yielding an average gain of 1.3% over previous methods.

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-01881-1.abstract: Abstract Emotion classification on social media provides valuable insights into public sentiment, but the performance of existing models is often limited by corpus size and linguistic variability. This research presents a transfer learning approach to analyze the benchmark EmoT corpus of 4401 emotion-labeled Indonesian Tweets, combined with a task-specific data augmentation strategy to enhance model generalization. Statistical analysis is performed using a linear mixed model of 10-fold cross validation folds, with folds modeled as a random intercept to control for within-fold variation. Results reveal that both Model and Augmentation Strategy have a significant effect on Accuracy, Macro F1, and Weighted F1 metrics. The top-performing model-strategy combination is IndoRoBERTa with augmentation via one-phase back translation, achieving a Weighted F1 score of approximately 0.859. These results highlight the effectiveness of integrating transfer learning with textual data augmentation for emotion classification in low-resource languages and suggest promising directions for future research in natural language processing.
doi:10.1007/s44163-026-01881-1.title: A transfer learning with data augmentation approach to emotion classification of Indonesian tweets

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-01924-7.abstract: Text-to-Speech synthesis has evolved from rule-based and concatenative systems to highly natural neural architectures. This review surveys the historical development of TTS, core system components, representative model families, benchmark datasets, and evaluation protocols. We summarize major advances in end-to-end neural TTS, non-autoregressive generation, neural vocoders, multilingual and expressive synthesis, and zero-shot voice cloning. We additionally discuss persistent challenges related to prosody control, low-resource languages, real-time inference, and ethical risks. Finally, we outline promising research directions in diffusion-based generation and speech-language foundation models for controllable and robust TTS.
doi:10.1007/s44163-026-01924-7.title: Comprehensive review of traditional and deep learning approaches to text to speech synthesis

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02243-7.abstract: Deploying trustworthy AI requires more than predictive accuracy; it demands population-representative data, transparent explainability, and user-centered design. Despite rapid mobile penetration across Southeast Asia, existing AI-based health tools remain predominantly trained on non-representative datasets and function as opaque black-box systems, limiting clinical trust. This study addresses these gaps through a deployable Explainable AI (XAI) framework for dysglycemia screening in Indonesia. Features were extracted from the Indonesia Family Life Survey 5 (IFLS5), a nationally representative longitudinal survey ( $$\sim $$ 83% of the Indonesian population), using its measured HbA1c-based labels for dysglycemia screening. Feature selection employed a four-stage XAI-in-the-loop pipeline combining literature review, statistical filtering, domain expert consultation, and SHAP-based evaluation. Among models trained, XGBoost achieved the highest performance (ROC-AUC = 0.72), with SHAP used both for post-hoc interpretation and feature selection. SHAP analysis indicated clinical alignment, with age, BMI, and hypertension as dominant risk factors, including a non-linear risk increase after age 45. The model was deployed as an Android application combining visual SHAP explanations with LLM-generated narratives. A pilot evaluation (n = 12) returned a mean comprehension score of 4.31/5. The framework illustrates an approach for developing transparent, population-representative mHealth AI that is meaningful and accessible to its intended users.

background.en:
Deploying trustworthy artificial intelligence in healthcare requires more than high predictive accuracy. It demands population-representative data, transparent explainability, and user-centered design to ensure clinical trust.

Despite rapid mobile penetration across Southeast Asia, existing AI-based health tools often rely on non-representative datasets and function as opaque black-box systems. This study addresses these critical gaps by developing a deployable Explainable AI framework for dysglycemia screening tailored to the Indonesian population.
background.id:
Penerapan kecerdasan buatan yang tepercaya dalam layanan kesehatan membutuhkan lebih dari sekadar akurasi prediktif yang tinggi. Hal ini menuntut data yang representatif bagi populasi, *explainability* yang transparan, dan desain yang berpusat pada pengguna untuk memastikan kepercayaan klinis.

Meskipun penetrasi seluler di Asia Tenggara berkembang pesat, perangkat kesehatan berbasis kecerdasan buatan saat ini sering kali mengandalkan *dataset* yang tidak representatif dan berfungsi sebagai sistem kotak hitam yang buram. Studi ini mengatasi kesenjangan krusial tersebut dengan mengembangkan *framework* *Explainable AI* yang dapat diterapkan untuk penapisan disglikemia yang disesuaikan dengan populasi Indonesia.

contributions.en:
The study introduces a deployable Explainable AI framework for dysglycemia screening that integrates population-representative data from a nationally representative longitudinal survey covering approximately 83 percent of the Indonesian population.

Furthermore, the work contributes a four-stage XAI-in-the-loop feature selection pipeline, clinical validation through SHAP analysis, and an end-user mobile application combining visual explanations with LLM-generated narratives, evaluated via a pilot study.

Studi ini memperkenalkan *framework* *Explainable AI* yang dapat diterapkan untuk penapisan disglikemia dengan mengintegrasikan data yang representatif secara nasional dari survei longitudinal yang mencakup sekitar 83 persen populasi Indonesia.

Selain itu, penelitian ini berkontribusi melalui *pipeline* seleksi fitur *XAI*-in-the-loop empat tahap, validasi klinis melalui analisis *SHAP*, serta aplikasi seluler bagi pengguna akhir yang menggabungkan penjelasan visual dengan narasi buatan *LLM*, yang dievaluasi melalui studi percontohan.

method.en:
Features were extracted from the Indonesia Family Life Survey 5, a nationally representative longitudinal survey utilizing measured HbA1c-based labels for dysglycemia screening. Feature selection was conducted using a four-stage Explainable AI in-the-loop pipeline that combined literature review, statistical filtering, domain expert consultation, and SHAP-based evaluation.

Several models were trained, with XGBoost achieving the highest performance. The best model was subsequently deployed as an Android application combining visual SHAP explanations with language model-generated narratives, followed by a pilot evaluation involving 12 participants.

Fitur diekstrak dari Indonesia Family Life Survey 5, sebuah survei longitudinal yang representatif secara nasional dengan menggunakan label berbasis HbA1c untuk penapisan disglikemia. Seleksi fitur dilakukan menggunakan *pipeline* *Explainable AI* *in-the-loop* empat tahap yang menggabungkan tinjauan pustaka, penyaringan statistik, konsultasi pakar domain, dan evaluasi berbasis *SHAP*.

Beberapa model dilatih, di mana *XGBoost* mencapai performa tertinggi. Model terbaik tersebut kemudian diterapkan sebagai aplikasi Android yang menggabungkan penjelasan visual *SHAP* dengan narasi buatan model bahasa, diikuti oleh evaluasi percontohan yang melibatkan 12 partisipan.

results.en:
Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance with an ROC-AUC of 0.72. SHAP analysis demonstrated strong clinical alignment, identifying age, body mass index, and hypertension as dominant risk factors, including a non-linear risk increase observed after age 45.

Additionally, a pilot evaluation involving 12 participants yielded a mean comprehension score of 4.31 out of 5, indicating that the visual explanations and language model narratives were well understood by the intended users.

Di antara model yang dievaluasi, *XGBoost* mencapai performa prediktif tertinggi dengan nilai ROC-AUC sebesar 0,72. Analisis *SHAP* menunjukkan keselarasan klinis yang kuat, dengan mengidentifikasi usia, indeks massa tubuh, dan hipertensi sebagai faktor risiko dominan, termasuk peningkatan risiko non-linear yang teramati setelah usia 45 tahun.

Selain itu, evaluasi percontohan yang melibatkan 12 partisipan menghasilkan skor pemahaman rata-rata 4,31 dari 5, yang mengindikasikan bahwa penjelasan visual dan narasi model bahasa dipahami dengan baik oleh pengguna yang dituju.

tldr.en: This study introduces a population-representative explainable AI framework for dysglycemia screening in Indonesia using data from the Indonesia Family Life Survey 5. The deployed mobile application combines XGBoost predictions with SHAP explanations and language model narratives, achieving high clinical alignment and user comprehension.

Aplikasi seluler yang diterapkan menggabungkan prediksi *XGBoost* dengan penjelasan *SHAP* dan narasi *large language model*, serta mencapai keselarasan klinis dan pemahaman pengguna yang tinggi.

doi:10.1007/s44196-026-01586-4.abstract: Analysis of communication across cultures is essential in global digital interactions, requiring models that capture linguistic and paralinguistic features across diverse cultures. However, existing studies lack privacy-preserving frameworks that can effectively model both linguistic and paralinguistic features across distributed and culturally diverse datasets, highlighting a critical research gap. Existing centralized approaches pose privacy risks and often fail to preserve cultural nuances in distributed communication data. This research presents a CAFL to integrate linguistic and paralinguistic features across multiple cultural groups while maintaining data decentralization. A culture-specific gradient aggregation strategy is introduced to reduce representation bias and improve performance in low-resource languages. Evaluation across 27 cultural groups shows 93.7% accuracy in communication pattern recognition and an 87.4% reduction in privacy risk compared to centralized methods. The model captures prosodic variations, conversational timing, and non-verbal cues often overlooked by conventional NLP techniques. The findings reveal new cross-cultural communication patterns and provide a scalable, privacy-aware solution for intercultural collaboration, global communication systems, and culturally adaptive AI.

doi:10.1007/s44354-026-00047-w.abstract: In particular, the rapid dissemination of fake news using social media platforms has posed a severe threat to social stability and information reliability in language groups that lack sufficient resources. In addition, it has become difficult to automatically identify fake news in the case of Bengali digital media because fake news is mostly distributed using multimodal data like memes, screenshots, posters, photos with texts, etc. The effectiveness of the existing fake news detection methods is somewhat hindered by their inability to provide explainability and their focus mainly on either textual or visual data. This study proposes a context-aware multimodal reasoning approach for explainable Bengali fake news detection. The proposed model incorporates EasyOCR for Bengali textual information extraction, ResNet-50 and ViT for supplementing visual feature learning, and Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct for multimodal semantic inference. The proposed approach can detect semantic contradictions and associations between textual assertions and image information through matching textual and visual data based on a context-sensitive fusion technique. This methodology generates interpretable explanations beyond the fake/real binary categorization to enhance user trust in automated outcomes. According to an experiment conducted using a multimodal Bengali fake news dataset, the proposed approach surpasses conventional CNN, transformer, and unimodal baselines on several performance metrics. Results indicate how context-based multimodal reasoning can improve the efficiency and robustness of the model, along with making it more interpretable. The proposed method serves as an encouraging route towards the identification of fake news in multiple low resource languages, as well as in combating misinformation in the Bengali digital ecosystem.

doi:10.1007/s44443-026-01019-4.abstract: Low-resource languages remain challenging for cross-lingual semantic alignment because of limited parallel corpora. In addition, conventional symmetric alignment may distort the semantic space of a high-resource language through noisy low-resource updates. To address this issue, we propose Monolingual Anchoring for Cross-Lingual Semantic Alignment (MACA), focusing on Uyghur as a low-resource case study. MACA follows an asymmetric paradigm that treats the high-resource language as a fixed semantic anchor and transfers its semantic structure to the Uyghur side. The method consists of three components: (1) Anchored Embedding Initialization for newly introduced Uyghur subwords, (2) Cross-Lingual Neighborhood Anchoring for structural alignment between Uyghur and the anchor language, and (3) Monolingual Structure Anchoring for improving the internal semantic organization of Uyghur representations. Experiments centered on Uyghur-Chinese show that MACA outperforms LaBSE, the strongest off-the-shelf multilingual baseline in our comparison, by 7.67 points on cross-lingual STS. In an exploratory Uyghur-English zero-shot setting, MACA also surpasses LaBSE by 2.45 points without using Uyghur-English training data. These results provide evidence for the effectiveness of MACA in the evaluated Uyghur setting and suggest that monolingual anchoring may be further explored for related low-resource languages, such as Kazakh, Kyrgyz, and Uzbek.
