doi:10.33395/jmp.v15i2.16581.abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital connectivity in Indonesia has catalyzed an unprecedented surge in harmful online content, necessitating robust automated systems for hate speech detection that can generalize across diverse digital platforms. Traditional models often struggle with domain shift and the linguistic complexities of Indonesian social media discourse, including informal slang and code-mixing. This research proposes a multi-domain detection framework leveraging the IndoBERT-base-p1 architecture integrated with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategy. The study utilizes a multi-source corpus from Instagram, Twitter, and news portals, employing back-translation to augment scarce Instagram data and stratified downsampling to ensure domain equilibrium. By training only 1–2% of the total 110 million parameters, specifically targeting the query and value attention modules, the model achieves significant computational savings with a training loss of 0.345. Experimental results demonstrate high robustness, with the framework attaining F1-scores of 0.83 for both Instagram and Twitter, and 0.81 for news portals, while maintaining accuracies between 0.81 and 0.85. Qualitative validation through word cloud analysis further confirms the model's ability to distinguish between aggressive sociopolitical triggers and neutral functional discourse. This study contributes a scalable and resource-efficient solution for real-time content moderation, proving effective across both formal journalistic Indonesian and informal digital dialects. The findings indicate that IndoBERT+LoRA provides a promising and resource-efficient approach for multi-domain Indonesian hate and abusive speech classification, while stricter leave-one-domain-out evaluation remains an important direction for future work.
doi:10.33395/jmp.v15i2.16581.title: Indonesian Hate Speech Detection Across Diverse Domains Using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with IndoBERT and LoRA

doi:10.33395/jmp.v15i3.16145.abstract: The Board of Peace is an international body initiated by U.S. President Donald Trump. The government’s decision to join this body has naturally sparked debate among the public, particularly on the social media platform X. The social media platform X (Twitter) is one of the best platforms for monitoring public opinion on various topics, including government policies—such as those implemented by President Prabowo Subianto. Twitter provides users with a space to follow the latest developments, participate in conversations, and express their opinions on public policy and leadership. In Indonesia, Twitter is frequently used for planning social events, sharing information, and voicing criticism or expectations toward national leaders. This study aims to analyze public sentiment regarding Indonesia’s joining the Board of Peace using the IndoBERT and NusaBERT algorithms. The dataset used, consisting of 290 data points, was obtained through data crawling techniques from the social media platform X. The research stages included Data Collection, Data Pre-Processing, Data Balancing, Fine-Tuning of the Transformer Model, and Model Evaluation (accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score). The results of this study show that the IndoBERT algorithm achieved an accuracy of 90%, while NusaBERT achieved an accuracy of 97%. This indicates that the NusaBERT algorithm has a 7% advantage in accuracy. This study underscores the importance of selecting the appropriate algorithm to enhance the performance of sentiment analysis systems on public policy topics.

glossary.explanation_id: Proses penyesuaian bobot pada *model bahasa* pralatih menggunakan *dataset* target tertentu.
Teknik pengumpulan data otomatis dari halaman web atau media sosial menggunakan skrip pemrogram.
Tahap penormalan teks untuk mengubah seluruh huruf kapital menjadi huruf kecil.
Prosedur penambahan sampel pada kelas minoritas untuk menyeimbangkan distribusi *dataset*.
Tabel evaluasi yang membandingkan prediksi model dengan label aktual untuk mengukur performa *klasifikasi*.
Metrik evaluasi yang mengukur ketepatan prediksi positif dari keseluruhan hasil prediksi positif.
Metrik evaluasi yang mengukur kemampuan model dalam menemukan kembali seluruh instans kelas positif.
Rata-rata harmonis dari *precision* dan *recall* yang memberikan ukuran performa *model* secara menyeluruh.

background.en:
The Indonesian government decision to join the Board of Peace, an international body initiated by U.S. President Donald Trump, has sparked widespread public debate. Monitoring public opinion regarding this government policy is essential for understanding societal perspectives. Platform X serves as a primary digital space where citizens voice opinions, criticisms, and expectations toward national leadership under President Prabowo Subianto.

Analyzing public sentiment from social media data presents challenges due to the volume and nuances of informal text. The paper addresses the need to evaluate how advanced transformer models process policy-related discourse in Indonesian, highlighting that algorithm selection directly impacts the performance of sentiment analysis systems.
background.id:
Keputusan pemerintah Indonesia untuk bergabung dengan *Board of Peace*, sebuah badan internasional yang diinisiasi oleh Presiden Amerika Serikat Donald Trump, telah memicu perdebatan luas di tengah masyarakat. Memantau opini publik mengenai kebijakan pemerintah ini sangat penting untuk memahami perspektif masyarakat. Platform X berfungsi sebagai ruang digital utama tempat warga menyuarakan pendapat, kritik, dan harapan terhadap kepemimpinan nasional di bawah Presiden Prabowo Subianto.

Menganalisis sentimen publik dari data media sosial menghadirkan tantangan karena volume dan nuansa teks informal. Makalah ini membahas kebutuhan untuk mengevaluasi bagaimana *model transformer* mutakhir memproses wacana terkait kebijakan dalam bahasa Indonesia, serta menekankan bahwa pemilihan algoritma berdampak langsung pada performa sistem analisis sentimen.

contributions.en:
The primary contribution of this research is a comparative evaluation of IndoBERT and NusaBERT applied specifically to public sentiment regarding Indonesia joining the Board of Peace. The study utilizes a crawled dataset from platform X subjected to a rigorous data preprocessing and balancing pipeline.

Additionally, the work provides empirical evidence showing the performance advantage of NusaBERT over IndoBERT in capturing regional language nuances within policy discussions. It establishes a clear benchmark for sentiment classification accuracy and metric evaluation in this specific geopolitical domain.
contributions.id:
Kontribusi utama dari penelitian ini adalah evaluasi komparatif antara *IndoBERT* dan *NusaBERT* yang diterapkan secara khusus pada sentimen publik mengenai bergabungnya Indonesia ke *Board of Peace*. Penelitian ini memanfaatkan *dataset* hasil *crawling* dari platform X yang melalui rangkaian *preprocessing* data dan penyeimbangan data yang ketat.

Selain itu, karya ini memberikan bukti empiris yang menunjukkan keunggulan performa *NusaBERT* atas *IndoBERT* dalam menangkap nuansa bahasa regional di dalam diskusi kebijakan. Penelitian ini menetapkan *benchmark* yang jelas untuk akurasi klasifikasi sentimen dan evaluasi metrik pada domain geopolitik khusus ini.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail.
future_work.id: Makalah tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan secara rinci.

method.en:
The research methodology follows a systematic pipeline consisting of problem identification, data collection, data preprocessing, data balancing, transformer model fine-tuning, and model evaluation. Data collection involved scraping 290 tweets from platform X using Tweet-Harvest via Node.js based on relevant keywords. The data was stored in CSV format and processed using Python in Google Colab.

Data preprocessing included cleaning to remove URLs, punctuation, hashtags, HTML tags, and symbols, followed by case folding and automated lexicon-based labeling into positive, negative, and neutral classes. To address class imbalance where the neutral class dominated, random oversampling was applied. The dataset was split into 80 percent training data and 20 percent testing data. Fine-tuning utilized HuggingFace Transformers and PyTorch for IndoBERT and NusaBERT, while evaluation metrics comprised accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score derived from a Multiclass Confusion Matrix 3x3.
method.id:
Metodologi penelitian mengikuti alur sistematis yang terdiri dari identifikasi masalah, pengumpulan data, *preprocessing* data, penyeimbangan data, *fine-tuning model transformer*, dan evaluasi model. Pengumpulan data melibatkan *scraping* 290 tweet dari platform X menggunakan *Tweet-Harvest* melalui *Node.js* berdasarkan kata kunci yang relevan. Data disimpan dalam format CSV dan diproses menggunakan *Python* di *Google Colab*.

*Preprocessing* data mencakup *cleaning* untuk menghapus URL, tanda baca, *hashtag*, tag HTML, dan simbol, dilanjutkan dengan *case folding* dan pelabelan otomatis berbasis *lexicon* ke dalam kelas positif, negatif, dan netral. Untuk mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas di mana kelas netral mendominasi, diterapkan *oversampling* acak. *Dataset* dibagi menjadi 80 persen data latih dan 20 persen data uji. *Fine-tuning* memanfaatkan *HuggingFace Transformers* dan *PyTorch* untuk *IndoBERT* dan *NusaBERT*, sementara metrik evaluasi mencakup *accuracy*, *precision*, *recall*, dan *F1-score* yang diperoleh dari *Multiclass Confusion Matrix* 3x3.

related_work.en:
The study builds upon prior research utilizing transformer models for sentiment analysis in Indonesian political and social contexts. Previous investigations applied IndoBERT to free nutritious meal policy sentiment and political hoax detection, achieving high accuracy rates. Other works explored NusaBERT for sentiment classification of football supporters and LGBT issues on platform X.

These prior studies demonstrated that models like IndoBERT and NusaBERT maintain robust baseline accuracies ranging from 70 percent to 90 percent. However, the authors note that comparative evaluations specifically targeting international policy decisions like the Board of Peace using these regional transformer variants remain necessary.
related_work.id:
Penelitian ini dibangun berdasarkan studi terdahulu yang memanfaatkan *model transformer* untuk analisis sentimen dalam konteks politik dan sosial di Indonesia. Investigasi sebelumnya menerapkan *IndoBERT* pada sentimen kebijakan makan bergizi gratis dan deteksi hoaks politik, serta mencapai tingkat akurasi yang tinggi. Karya lain mengeksplorasi *NusaBERT* untuk klasifikasi sentimen suporter sepak bola dan isu LGBT di platform X.

Studi-studi terdahulu ini menunjukkan bahwa model seperti *IndoBERT* dan *NusaBERT* mempertahankan akurasi dasar yang andal pada kisaran 70 persen hingga 90 persen. Namun, para penulis mencatat bahwa evaluasi komparatif yang secara khusus menargetkan keputusan kebijakan internasional seperti *Board of Peace* menggunakan varian *transformer* regional ini masih tetap diperlukan.

results.en:
The experimental results demonstrate that NusaBERT outperforms IndoBERT across all evaluated performance metrics. NusaBERT achieved an accuracy of 0.97 or 97 percent, a precision of 0.99, a recall of 0.90, and an F1-score of 0.94. In contrast, IndoBERT achieved an accuracy of 0.90 or 90 percent, a precision of 0.63, a recall of 0.57, and an F1-score of 0.59.

The authors interpret these findings as proof that NusaBERT possesses a 7 percent accuracy advantage and is more effective at representing the dataset. This performance difference highlights the significance of utilizing models trained on specific regional language data when analyzing public policy sentiment.
results.id:
Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa *NusaBERT* unggul daripada *IndoBERT* pada semua metrik performa yang dievaluasi. *NusaBERT* mencapai akurasi sebesar 0,97 atau 97 persen, *precision* 0,99, *recall* 0,90, dan *F1-score* 0,94. Sebaliknya, *IndoBERT* mencapai akurasi sebesar 0,90 atau 90 persen, *precision* 0,63, *recall* 0,57, dan *F1-score* 0,59.

Para penulis menginterpretasikan temuan ini sebagai bukti bahwa *NusaBERT* memiliki keunggulan akurasi sebesar 7 persen dan lebih efektif dalam merepresentasikan *dataset*. Perbedaan performa ini menyoroti signifikansi penggunaan model yang dilatih pada data bahasa regional tertentu saat menganalisis sentimen kebijakan publik.

tldr.en: This study analyzes public sentiment on platform X regarding Indonesia joining the Board of Peace using IndoBERT and NusaBERT models. The results demonstrate that NusaBERT achieves a superior accuracy of 97 percent compared to IndoBERT at 90 percent.
tldr.id: Penelitian ini menganalisis sentimen publik pada platform X terkait bergabungnya Indonesia ke *Board of Peace* menggunakan model *IndoBERT* dan *NusaBERT*. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa *NusaBERT* mencapai akurasi yang lebih unggul sebesar 97 persen dibandingkan *IndoBERT* sebesar 90 persen.

doi:10.33395/jmp.v15i3.16145.title: Analisis Perspektif Mengenai Kebijakan Pemerintah Bergabung Dengan Board Of Peace Menggunakan IndoBERT dan NusaBERT

doi:10.33395/sinkron.v10i3.16294.abstract: Depression has become a major mental health issue in Indonesia, where approximately 167 million of the country’s 273 million citizens actively use social media platforms such as X (Twitter). The informal writing style, code-mixing, and linguistic variability in Indonesian tweets create significant challenges for automated depression detection systems. This study evaluates a fine-tuned IndoBERT model combined with a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier for detecting depression-related indications from Indonesian-language tweets. A total of 10,082 Indonesian tweets were collected and labeled into two categories: Terindikasi Depresi and Tidak Terindikasi; after deduplication, 3,874 unique tweets were used for modeling. Two scenarios were compared: (1) a fine-tuned IndoBERT model, and (2) fine-tuned IndoBERT CLS embeddings with a linear SVM classifier. The fine-tuned IndoBERT model achieved 73.20% accuracy (AUC-ROC = 0.8212), while the hybrid approach achieved a marginally higher 73.71% accuracy (AUC-ROC = 0.8088); a McNemar’s test found this difference not statistically significant (p = 0.86). Both models outperformed five traditional TF-IDF-based baselines (best: 70.36%) on the same held-out test set. The hybrid model required only 0.01 MB of storage versus 475.24 MB for the full fine-tuned model. Given statistically equivalent accuracy, combining fine-tuned IndoBERT embeddings with SVM offers substantially lower storage requirements at no measurable cost in classification performance, making it a promising, resource-efficient approach for depression detection on Indonesian social media.
doi:10.33395/sinkron.v10i3.16294.title: Depression Detection on Indonesian Social Media Using Fine-Tuned IndoBERT and SVM

doi:10.33480/jitk.v12i1.8222.abstract: Research on sarcasm detection in sentences generally focuses on English and the national languages of certain countries, so that regional languages such as Palembang are still underrepresented in NLP research. This study aims to classify sarcasm in Palembang sentences by applying 12 models and evaluating their performance using a dataset containing 1,952 manually annotated samples. The experiment was also conducted using a 5-fold cross-validation scheme, and the statistical significance of the test results was analyzed using the Friedman t-test ( =41.96, FF=12.90). Contrary to common expectations, the Ensemble classifier achieved the best overall performance, attaining a mean F1-score of 0.877 and outperforming larger pre-trained and dialect-specific models. Even though it is still in the same language family, MelayuBERT's performance is very far behind (F1:0.691). Furthermore, the relatively lower performance of IndoBERT-1.5G (0.731) suggests that model scale alone does not guarantee effectiveness in low-resource language settings. These findings highlight the robustness of feature-engineered classical models compared to large-scale or dialect-specific pre-trained models for sarcasm detection in low-resource regional languages. Our research results with datasets sourced from varied domains have exceeded several national benchmarks. This study can be a baseline for further research.

doi:10.33480/jitk.v12i1.8222.title: SARCASM DETECTION IN PALEMBANG LANGUAGE USING HYBRID CLASSICAL AND DEEP LEARNING APPROACHES

doi:10.33480/jitk.v12i1.8327.abstract: Sentiment analysis of hospital patient reviews plays a critical role in evaluating healthcare service quality. However, limited labeled data and class imbalance often affect classification performance and reduce minority-class detection. This study empirically investigates the impact of text augmentation techniques on improving IndoBERT performance for sentiment classification of patient reviews at Dr. Mohammad Hoesin Palembang General Hospital. A total of 1,464 reviews were collected, preprocessed, and weakly labeled using a VADER-based approach, resulting in 1,168 positive and 296 negative instances. To address class imbalance, augmentation was applied exclusively to the training set using back-translation and Easy Data Augmentation (EDA), including synonym replacement, random insertion, random swap, and random deletion. IndoBERT was fine-tuned under consistent hyperparameter settings and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-macro, and AUC. The baseline model achieved an F1-macro of 70.2%, indicating limited minority-class sensitivity. After augmentation, the random swap technique achieved the highest observed performance within the experimental setup, reaching 96.8% accuracy, 95.3% F1-macro, and 98.9% AUC. These results suggest improved performance within the experimental setting, particularly in minority-class detection. However, it should be noted that the labels were generated through a translation-based weak labeling approach, which may introduce noise and affect the accuracy of the labels. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted within the scope of this experimental setting.

doi:10.33480/jitk.v12i1.8327.title: IMPACT OF TEXT AUGMENTATION ON INDOBERT PERFORMANCE FOR HOSPITAL REVIEW SENTIMENT ANALYSIS
doi:10.33480/jitk.v12i1.8327.venue: JITK (Jurnal Ilmu Pengetahuan dan Teknologi Komputer)

doi:10.33545/26646021.2026.v8.i9b.1282.abstract: Critical scholarship increasingly characterizes the global expansion of artificial intelligence as a contin-uation of colonialism, a description which is politically serviceable and analytically loose. Technologyfirms hold no territory, command no armed force and exercise no legal sovereignty over other states, soequating platform capitalism with territorial conquest reduces colonialism to a metaphor. The defensiblecomparison is not with colonialism but with coloniality, the durable patterns of hierarchy and depen-dence which outlasted formal empire. Proceeding from that distinction, the article disaggregates a claimwhich is ordinarily made whole. Algorithmic bias is traced through four separable stages, from pretrain-ing corpora through representation and alignment to deployment, each of which admits a different rem-edy. Linguistic disadvantage is located in the mechanics of tokenization rather than cultural preference,which converts a symbolic harm into a measurable quantity. The Global South is disaggregated by statecapacity, and Southern states treated as potential agents of digital control rather than only its subjects.Digital labor is separated into data subjects, annotators and low-resource language communities, whoseinterests do not coincide. Fanon's account of psychic alienation is retained as a hypothesis which re-quires validation. A paradox in the proposed remedies is identified, model sovereignty is attainablewithout computer sovereignty, and sovereign artificial intelligence built on rented infrastructure relo-cates dependency without reducing it. A six-dimension framework with named indicators is offered sothat competing claims may be assessed rather than asserted.

doi:10.33545/26646021.2026.v8.i9b.1282.title: Reframing digital colonialism in Global South AIgovernance
doi:10.33545/26646021.2026.v8.i9b.1282.venue: International Journal of Political Science and Governance

doi:10.33545/27076571.2026.v7.i8a.364.abstract: Parts-of-Speech (PoS) tagging and Named Entity Recognition (NER) are fundamental tasks in Natural Language Processing (NLP), supporting downstream applications such as machine translation, information extraction, and sentiment analysis. While these tasks have achieved strong performance in high-resource languages like English, many low-resource languages remain underexplored due to the lack of annotated corpora and computational tools. Tulu - a Dravidian language spoken in coastal Karnataka, India - is one such language, with only limited work on PoS tagging as well as NER. To address this gap, in this paper, we present manually constructed Tulu datasets annotated with 18 PoS tags and 37 NER tags for PoS Tagging and NER respectively. We establish baselines using traditional Machine Learning (ML) algorithms trained with feature fusion of handcrafted features and character embeddings, as well as hybrid models that combine Deep Learning (DL) architectures with Conditional Random Field (CRF). This hybrid design integrates both character and word embeddings to capture richer contextual and morphological information. While the DL component learns long-range dependencies in sequential data, CRF layer ensures globally consistent and valid label sequences by modeling dependencies among output tags. Results demonstrate that hybrid models consistently outperform traditional approaches for both PoS tagging and NER. In summary, this study introduces the first Tulu PoS and NER datasets and strong baselines, laying the foundation for future NLP research in Tulu.
