doi:10.33545/27076571.2026.v7.i8a.364.title: Exploring low-resource Tulu NLP: A case study of PoS tagging and NER
doi:10.33545/27076571.2026.v7.i8a.364.venue: International Journal of Computing and Artificial Intelligence

doi:10.33578/kpd.v5i3.p329-343.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan alat evaluasi berbasis game edukasi menggunakan aplikasi Quizizz pada mata pelajaran Bahasa Indonesia kelas VIII di SMP Negeri 21 Makassar. Pengembangan dilakukan untuk menjawab kebutuhan guru dan siswa terhadap alat evaluasi yang lebih interaktif, menarik, dan efisien dibandingkan evaluasi konvensional. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Research and Development (R&D) dengan model ADDIE yang meliputi tahap Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, dan Evaluation. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas siswa kelas VIII dan guru Bahasa Indonesia SMP Negeri 21 Makassar. Teknik pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui wawancara, angket, tes, dan dokumentasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa siswa dan guru memiliki kebutuhan yang tinggi terhadap penggunaan Quizizz sebagai alat evaluasi pembelajaran. Produk yang dikembangkan divalidasi oleh ahli media dengan persentase 96,6% dan ahli materi sebesar 96% sehingga termasuk kategori sangat valid. Hasil uji coba kelompok kecil memperoleh persentase 91,3% dan uji coba kelompok besar memperoleh persentase 91,1% yang termasuk kategori sangat praktis. Hasil tanggapan guru juga menunjukkan respons yang sangat positif terhadap penggunaan media. Dengan demikian, alat evaluasi berbasis game edukasi menggunakan Quizizz dinyatakan valid dan praktis digunakan sebagai alternatif evaluasi pembelajaran Bahasa Indonesia kelas VIII SMP Negeri 21 Makassar
doi:10.33578/kpd.v5i3.p329-343.title: Pengembangan Alat Evaluasi Berbasis Game Edukasi Pada Mata Pelajaran Bahasa Indonesia Kelas VIII di SMP Negeri 21 Makassar

doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1856286.abstract: Introduction Mental health triage-level intent classification in linguistically diverse and resource-constrained clinical environments requires models that simultaneously meet strict patient data privacy regulations, cross-lingual generalization to low-resource languages, and real-time inference on edge hardware. No existing federated NLP system has jointly demonstrated this combination. This work proposes Fed-XLM-R, a unified federated learning framework designed to close that gap. Methods Fed-XLM-R integrates XLM-RoBERTa with lightweight bottleneck adapter layers, adapter-scoped differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD), proximal regularization for straggler-robust aggregation (FedProx), and INT8 post-training quantization for edge deployment. Gradient perturbation is confined exclusively to the 0.87% trainable adapter subspace rather than the full 270-million-parameter model. The framework was evaluated in a simulated 10-client federation on a public benchmark, with intent classification trained and evaluated on English data. A cross-lingual diagnostic was additionally run on the XNLI benchmark across five languages (English, Spanish, Hindi, Swahili, Arabic) against an mBERT baseline, and canary phrase memorization analysis was conducted across all 50 federated rounds to assess data extraction risk. Results At the clinically meaningful privacy budget of ε = 1.0 ( δ = 10 −5 , Fed-XLM-R achieves 96% accuracy retention, yielding an overall accuracy of 0.923, F1-score of 0.918, and AUC-ROC of 0.956, within 0.5% of a centralized baseline while providing formal differential privacy guarantees. Canary phrase analysis confirms the DP-SGD mechanism prevents training data extraction. The XLM-R backbone retains strong discriminative capacity in low-resource languages relative to mBERT on the XNLI diagnostic. Adapter-only parameter transmission reduces cumulative communication cost by 40.7-fold at the 85% accuracy threshold, at a per-round volume compatible with standard mobile data networks. INT8 quantization reduces inference latency from 1,974 ms to 523 ms on low-end CPU hardware, a 3.8-fold speedup. Discussion These findings characterize the mechanism's behavior under controlled conditions in a simulated federation rather than demonstrating field deployment. The cross-lingual results support the feasibility of future multilingual extension but do not themselves constitute multilingual intent classification. The three-category label scheme (Anxiety/Depression/Normal) supports triage-level intent routing but has not been validated against standardized clinical instruments; the system is not proposed as a clinical diagnostic or screening tool. Overall, Fed-XLM-R demonstrates that privacy-preserving, communication-efficient, and edge-deployable federated NLP is achievable without substantial accuracy loss, offering a practical pathway toward privacy-compliant mental health triage systems pending real-world and multilingual validation.

glossary.explanation_id: *Federated learning* adalah pendekatan pelatihan *machine learning* secara terdesentralisasi di mana model dilatih di berbagai perangkat atau klien lokal tanpa membagikan data mentah mereka.
*Differential privacy* adalah kerangka kerja matematis untuk memberikan jaminan privasi yang ketat dengan menambahkan *noise* yang dikalibrasi ke dalam pembaruan model.
*Adapter* adalah modul parameter kecil yang disisipkan di antara lapisan *transformer* untuk melakukan *fine-tuning* yang efisien tanpa mengubah bobot dasar model.
*Quantization* adalah proses mengurangi presisi numerik bobot model, misalnya dari *floating-point* 32-bit ke bilangan bulat 8-bit, untuk mempercepat inferensi dan menghemat memori.
Data *non-IID* mengacu pada distribusi data antar klien yang tidak independen dan tidak identik, sehingga mencerminkan heterogenitas dunia nyata.
*Proximal regularization* adalah teknik penalti dalam fungsi objektif lokal untuk mencegah pembaruan klien menyimpang terlalu jauh dari model global.
*Inference latency* adalah waktu yang dibutuhkan oleh model terlatih untuk memproses input dan menghasilkan prediksi.
*Straggler* adalah perangkat klien yang lebih lambat dalam menyelesaikan komputasi lokal dibandingkan dengan klien lainnya dalam jaringan *federated*.

background.en: Mental health triage-level intent classification in resource-constrained and linguistically diverse clinical environments requires balancing strict patient privacy regulations, cross-lingual generalization to low-resource languages, and real-time inference on edge hardware. Existing federated NLP systems typically treat these requirements as separate objectives rather than jointly optimizing them, and they often lack formal privacy guarantees against gradient inference attacks while failing to support low-resource clinical languages.
background.id: Klasifikasi niat tingkat *triage* kesehatan mental di lingkungan klinis yang memiliki keterbatasan sumber daya dan keragaman linguistik memerlukan keseimbangan antara regulasi privasi pasien yang ketat, generalisasi lintas bahasa ke bahasa *low-resource*, dan inferensi waktu nyata pada perangkat *edge*. Sistem *federated* NLP yang ada biasanya memperlakukan persyaratan ini sebagai tujuan yang terpisah alih-alih mengoptimalkannya secara bersamaan, serta sering kali tidak memiliki jaminan privasi formal terhadap serangan inferensi *gradient* dan gagal mendukung bahasa klinis *low-resource*.

contributions.en: The paper introduces Fed-XLM-R, which makes four main contributions: an adapter-scoped DP-SGD strategy restricting gradient perturbation to the 0.87% trainable parameter subspace, a joint DP-FedProx local update rule ensuring sample-level privacy and straggler robustness, an XLM-R backbone evaluated via cross-lingual XNLI diagnostics across five languages, and a pipeline combining adapter-only communication reduction with INT8 post-training quantization for edge deployment.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memperkenalkan Fed-XLM-R yang memberikan empat kontribusi utama: strategi DP-SGD berbasis *adapter* yang membatasi perturbasi *gradient* pada subspesparameter *trainable* sebesar 0,87%, aturan pembaruan lokal DP-FedProx gabungan yang memastikan privasi tingkat sampel dan ketahanan terhadap *straggler*, *backbone* XLM-R yang dievaluasi melalui diagnostik lintas bahasa XNLI di lima bahasa, serta *pipeline* yang menggabungkan pengurangan komunikasi khusus *adapter* dengan kuantisasi *post-training* INT8 untuk penerapan pada *edge*.

future_work.en: The authors note several limitations, including the simulated nature of the 10-client federation rather than a real multi-institutional deployment, training intent classification exclusively in English, the lack of clinical validation against standardized instruments like PHQ-9 or GAD-7, and the need to extend language coverage to other low-resource languages such as Bengali, Hausa, and Amharic.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat beberapa keterbatasan, termasuk sifat simulasi dari federasi 10 klien alih-alih penerapan nyata multi-institusi, pelatihan klasifikasi niat yang hanya menggunakan bahasa Inggris, kurangnya validasi klinis terhadap instrumen terstandarisasi seperti PHQ-9 atau GAD-7, serta kebutuhan untuk memperluas cakupan bahasa ke bahasa *low-resource* lain seperti Bengali, Hausa, dan Amharic.

method.en: The framework uses XLM-R as the base encoder equipped with Houlsby bottleneck adapters across all 12 layers while freezing base weights. Training is conducted in a simulated federation of 10 clients using a Dirichlet data partition. Clients perform local updates using DP-SGD with per-sample gradient clipping and calibrated Gaussian noise, combined with FedProx for proximal regularization. Following 50 rounds of federated training, the model undergoes INT8 post-training quantization and is evaluated on English Mental Health Q&A and cross-lingual XNLI benchmarks.
method.id: Kerangka kerja ini menggunakan XLM-R sebagai *encoder* dasar yang dilengkapi dengan *bottleneck adapter* Houlsby di seluruh 12 lapisan sementara bobot dasarnya dibekukan. Pelatihan dilakukan dalam simulasi federasi 10 klien menggunakan partisi data Dirichlet. Klien melakukan pembaruan lokal menggunakan DP-SGD dengan *gradient clipping* per sampel dan *noise* Gaussian terkalibrasi, dikombinasikan dengan FedProx untuk regularisasi proksimal. Setelah 50 putaran pelatihan *federated*, model menjalani kuantisasi *post-training* INT8 dan dievaluasi pada *benchmark* Mental Health Q&A berbahasa Inggris serta XNLI lintas bahasa.

related_work.en: Prior studies in healthcare NLP have explored federated learning for rare disease prediction, medical Q&A, and synthetic text generation, but they often lack formal differential privacy or cross-lingual support. Other privacy-preserving methods apply differential privacy or homomorphic encryption to medical imaging and signal data, while works like DP-Prox investigate differentially private fine-tuning for language models on edge devices without addressing cross-lingual transfer or clinical domains.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya dalam bidang NLP kesehatan telah mengeksplorasi *federated learning* untuk prediksi penyakit langka, tanya jawab medis, dan pembuatan teks sintetis, namun sering kali tidak memiliki *differential privacy* formal atau dukungan lintas bahasa. Metode penjagaan privasi lainnya menerapkan *differential privacy* atau *homomorphic encryption* pada pencitraan medis dan data sinyal, sementara penelitian seperti DP-Prox menyelidiki *fine-tuning* yang menjaga privasi untuk *language model* pada *edge device* tanpa mengatasi transfer lintas bahasa atau domain klinis.

results.en: At a privacy budget of epsilon equals 1.0, Fed-XLM-R achieves an overall accuracy of 0.923, an F1-score of 0.918, and an AUC-ROC of 0.956, which is within 0.5% of the centralized non-private baseline. Canary phrase analysis confirms that DP-SGD prevents training data memorization. Furthermore, adapter-only parameter transmission reduces cumulative communication cost by 40.7-fold, and INT8 quantization accelerates inference latency on low-end CPU hardware from 1,974 ms to 523 ms.
results.id: Pada anggaran privasi epsilon sama dengan 1,0, Fed-XLM-R mencapai akurasi keseluruhan 0,923, skor F1 0,918, dan AUC-ROC 0,956, yang berada dalam kisaran 0,5% dari *baseline* terpusat non-privat. Analisis *canary phrase* mengonfirmasi bahwa DP-SGD mencegah memorisasi data pelatihan. Selain itu, transmisi parameter khusus *adapter* mengurangi biaya komunikasi kumulatif hingga 40,7 kali lipat, dan kuantisasi INT8 mempercepat latensi inferensi pada perangkat keras CPU kelas bawah dari 1.974 ms menjadi 523 ms.

tldr.en: This paper proposes Fed-XLM-R, a unified federated framework for mental health triage intent classification that integrates adapter-scoped differential privacy, proximal regularization, and quantization. The method achieves high accuracy retention and strong privacy guarantees while operating efficiently on edge devices.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan Fed-XLM-R, sebuah *framework* *federated learning* terpadu untuk klasifikasi niat *triage* kesehatan mental yang mengintegrasikan *differential privacy* berbasis *adapter*, regularisasi proksimal, dan kuantisasi. Metode ini mencapai retensi akurasi yang tinggi serta jaminan privasi yang kuat sambil beroperasi secara efisien pada *edge device*.

doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1856286.title: Fed-XLM-R: a privacy-preserving federated framework with adapter-scoped differential privacy for mental health triage-level intent classification on resource-constrained edge devices

doi:10.3389/fpos.2026.1721896.abstract: Introduction Digital democracy in Indonesia increasingly unfolds through government-citizen interactions on social media platforms, yet the cognitive-discursive mechanisms underlying citizens’ responses to ministerial communication remain underexplored. This study examines how affective sentiment, ideological crystallization, and linguistic representation shape democratic engagement across social-essential policy sectors. Methods Employing a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design integrating BERT/ALBERT sentiment classification, netnographic interpretation, and corpus linguistics, we analyzed 4,950 Instagram comments posted during April 2025 on the verified accounts of four Indonesian social-essential ministries (Religious Affairs, Education, Health, and Manpower), approximately six months into the “Merah Putih” cabinet’s tenure following its inauguration on 21 October 2024. Results Sentiment analysis revealed substantial sectoral variation: Education received 72% positive sentiment, while Health and Manpower received 32% and 30% negative responses, respectively. Positive-sentiment communities employed gratitude discourse emphasizing governmental achievements, whereas negative-sentiment communities articulated structural critiques focused on inequality and institutional failure. Cross-cutting deliberation remained minimal, with within-sentiment replies outnumbering cross-sentiment replies by a ratio of 20:1, indicating strong echo-chamber dynamics. Corpus linguistic analysis demonstrated that ministerial representation through collocational patterns correlated strongly with sentiment distributions ( ρ = 0.94). Discussion Findings indicate that digital democratic engagement in Indonesia operates through layered cognitive-discursive mechanisms in which initial affective responses filter subsequent ideological positioning, which materializes linguistically in patterns of ministerial representation. The observed echo chamber dynamics, characterized by minimal cross-cutting deliberation, challenge Instagram’s capacity to function as a platform for democratic deliberation. These results contribute to an integrated cognitive-discursive framework linking affective sentiment, ideological crystallization, and linguistic materialization, with implications for digital governance strategies in developing democracies.
doi:10.3389/fpos.2026.1721896.title: Cognitive, discursive mechanisms of digital democracy in Indonesia: from sentiment to ideology

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1875268.abstract: The process of stemming is a fundamental part of pre-processing in NLP systems in resource-poor and morphologically complex languages in which linguistic data and annotated corpora are limited. This survey presents a a systematic review of stemming techniques across Afro-Asiatic, Indo-Aryan, Turkic, and Uralic language families, with explicit acknowledgment of coverage limitation and it covers rule-based, statistical, unsupervised, hybrid, and emerging neural-assisted approaches. The evolution of stemming is analyzed in the broader context of NLP paradigms, from early suffix-stripping algorithms to modern sub-word-aware and transformer-influenced models. Special emphasis has been given on resource-poor languages such as Arabic, Urdu, Bengali, Assamese, and other low-resource Indo-Aryan, Afro-Asiatic, and agglutinative languages. For these languages performing explicit stemming remains a critical task despite advances in deep learning. This study further reviews application-driven impacts of stemming in information retrieval, text classification, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and semantic similarity estimation. A unified comparison framework is presented which has incorporated benchmark datasets, shared-task resources, and multi-dimensional evaluation metrics, including precision, recall, F-measure, MAP, NMI, and stemming-specific error indices. Using careful comparative evaluation, this study points out the strengths and weaknesses of current approaches and provides insights into potential areas for future investigation and developments in language-sensitive stemming systems.

glossary.explanation_id: Proses mereduksi kata berimbuhan menjadi bentuk kata dasar dalam *natural language processing*.
Kumpulan teks besar yang terstruktur yang digunakan untuk analisis linguistik dan pelatihan *model bahasa*.
Metode *stemming* berbasis aturan yang bekerja dengan menghapus akhiran dari suatu kata.
Unit teks yang lebih kecil dari satu kata penuh, sering digunakan oleh *tokenizer* modern.
Arsitektur *deep learning* yang mengandalkan mekanisme *attention* untuk memproses data sekuensial.
Standar atau *dataset* standar yang digunakan untuk mengukur dan membandingkan performa berbagai *model*.
Proporsi prediksi positif yang benar dari keseluruhan hasil yang diprediksi positif oleh *model*.
Proporsi sampel positif aktual yang berhasil dideteksi dengan benar oleh *model*.

background.en: The process of stemming is a fundamental part of pre-processing in natural language processing systems, particularly for resource-poor and morphologically complex languages where linguistic data and annotated corpora are limited. Despite advancements in deep learning, performing explicit stemming remains a critical task for languages such as Arabic, Urdu, Bengali, Assamese, and other low-resource Indo-Aryan, Afro-Asiatic, and agglutinative languages.
background.id: Proses *stemming* merupakan bagian fundamental dari pra-pemrosesan dalam sistem *natural language processing*, terutama untuk bahasa yang termasuk *resource-poor* dan memiliki kompleksitas morfologis di mana data linguistik serta *korpus* beranotasi sangat terbatas. Meskipun ada kemajuan dalam *deep learning*, pelaksanaan *stemming* secara eksplisit tetap menjadi tugas krusial untuk bahasa seperti bahasa Arab, Urdu, Bengali, Assamese, serta bahasa Indo-Aryan, Afro-Asiatic, dan aglutinatif *low-resource* lainnya.

contributions.en: This survey presents a systematic review of stemming techniques across Afro-Asiatic, Indo-Aryan, Turkic, and Uralic language families, with explicit acknowledgment of coverage limitation. It covers rule-based, statistical, unsupervised, hybrid, and emerging neural-assisted approaches, while analyzing the evolution of stemming from early suffix-stripping algorithms to modern sub-word-aware and transformer-influenced models.
contributions.id: Survei ini menyajikan tinjauan sistematis mengenai teknik *stemming* di rumpun bahasa Afro-Asiatic, Indo-Aryan, Turkic, dan Uralic dengan pengakuan eksplisit terhadap batasan cakupan. Studi ini mencakup pendekatan *rule-based*, statistik, *unsupervised*, hibrida, dan *neural-assisted* yang sedang berkembang, sekaligus menganalisis evolusi *stemming* dari algoritma *suffix-stripping* awal hingga model modern yang sadar *sub-word* dan dipengaruhi *transformer*.

future_work.en: The study provides insights into potential areas for future investigation and developments in language-sensitive stemming systems.
future_work.id: Studi ini memberikan wawasan mengenai potensi area untuk investigasi dan pengembangan lebih lanjut pada sistem *stemming* yang sensitif terhadap bahasa.

method.en: The study reviews stemming techniques by analyzing their evolution within the broader context of natural language processing paradigms. It evaluates a unified comparison framework that incorporates benchmark datasets, shared-task resources, and multi-dimensional evaluation metrics, including precision, recall, F-measure, MAP, NMI, and stemming-specific error indices.
method.id: Studi ini meninjau teknik *stemming* dengan menganalisis evolusinya dalam konteks paradigma *natural language processing* yang lebih luas. Penelitian ini mengevaluasi kerangka perbandingan terpadu yang menggabungkan *dataset* *benchmark*, sumber daya *shared-task*, serta *metrik* evaluasi multi-dimensi termasuk *precision*, *recall*, *F-measure*, *MAP*, *NMI*, dan indeks kesalahan khusus *stemming*.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan terkait secara rinci.

results.en: Using careful comparative evaluation, the study points out the strengths and weaknesses of current approaches across various tasks. Furthermore, it reviews the application-driven impacts of stemming in information retrieval, text classification, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and semantic similarity estimation.
results.id: Menggunakan evaluasi perbandingan yang cermat, studi ini menunjukkan kelebihan dan kekurangan dari pendekatan saat ini di berbagai tugas. Lebih lanjut, penelitian ini meninjau dampak berbasis aplikasi dari *stemming* dalam *information retrieval*, *text classification*, *sentiment analysis*, *topic modeling*, dan *semantic similarity estimation*.

tldr.en: This paper presents a systematic review of stemming techniques for resource-poor and morphologically complex languages across multiple language families. It evaluates rule-based, statistical, unsupervised, hybrid, and neural-assisted approaches alongside their application-driven impacts.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan tinjauan sistematis mengenai teknik *stemming* untuk bahasa yang termasuk *resource-poor* dan memiliki kompleksitas morfologis di berbagai rumpun bahasa. Studi ini mengevaluasi pendekatan *rule-based*, statistik, *unsupervised*, hibrida, dan *neural-assisted* beserta dampaknya yang didorong oleh aplikasi.

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1875268.title: Stemming techniques for resource-poor languages: a review of methods, challenges, and applications

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1883049.abstract: Online voice-based applications and speech communication have grown as a result of the revolutionary rise of smart gadgets and social media. The rapid advancement of deep learning (DL) has transformed the field of audio processing, enabling smooth human-computer interaction. DL approaches have been used to develop speech-to-text (STT) systems across various languages and topics. These models require a large amount of training data: extensive corpora of continuous speech utterances collected from numerous speakers, along with their corresponding transcripts. In this study, we explore the use of state-of-the-art pre-trained models like Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53 and Whisper-small for developing STT systems in the Telugu language, addressing the challenge of limited data availability and demonstrating satisfactory results [23.62% Word Error Rate (WER), 4.12% Character Error Rate (CER)] even when fine-tuned on a smaller dataset. To evaluate model performance, we employed a k-fold cross-validation approach with values of k = 2 to k = 5, and compared the results with the conventional train-test split method. The results indicate that at k = 5, the Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53 model achieved a cross-validation Character Error Rate(WER) of 23.62% and a Character Error Rate (CER) of 4.12%, and the Whisper-small model yielded a cross-validation WER of 28.67% and a CER of 5.48%. These findings suggest that the k-fold cross-validation strategy, at k = 5, enhances the robustness of Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53 in low-resource language scenarios where training data is limited. For Whisper-small, however, the baseline train-test split (WER: 27.76%) outperformed all k-fold configurations tested (k = 2: 32.05%, k = 3: 29.72%, k = 4: 29.40%, k = 5: 28.67%), indicating that the benefit of k-fold cross-validation observed for Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53 does not generalize across model architectures. Additionally, the models were evaluated on unseen noisy data, and both models demonstrated satisfactory performance.
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1883049.title: Exploring Wav2Vec2 XLSR-53 and Whisper-small for Telugu language speech-to-text: a fine-tuning approach

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1905680.abstract: Text normalization (TN) is a crucial preprocessing task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that enables the conversion of noisy, informal texts into standardized forms suitable for downstream applications, such as machine translation, speech recognition, text-to-speech systems, sentiment analysis, and information retrieval. User-Generated Content (UGC) from social media and messaging platforms often contains irregularities such as abbreviations, phonetic spellings, code-switching, and orthographic inconsistencies. These irregularities have significant implications, especially for low-resourced languages like Hausa, which have limited annotated corpora and computational resources. Existing rule-based and statistical methods struggle in their performance with Hausa text because of spelling variations, code-mixing, abbreviations, and contextual ambiguities. In contrast, neural networks like transformers require a large dataset for efficient training; however, the lack of specialized resources like a parallel corpus further worsens the inefficiency of current models in handling Hausa UGC. To address these gaps, two corpora were developed: a Hausa UGC corpus collected from Twitter and WhatsApp, and a standard Hausa corpus consisting of 27,847 sentences each. The UGC corpus was analyzed to identify Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) words, their features, and usage patterns. A Dual-BERT Adversarial Network model was then designed and trained to map non-standard Hausa words into their canonical forms accurately. The developed model integrates dual-BERT within an adversarial learning framework, enabling it to capture both the semantic and contextual relationships between informal and standard text. One BERT processes noisy, user-generated Hausa input, while the other learns from standard Hausa sentences, allowing the system to model bidirectional correspondences between the two linguistic forms. Their representations are fused and refined through a generator-discriminator architecture, where the generator produces normalized outputs and the discriminator enforces contextual correctness by distinguishing genuine standard text from generated ones. This adversarial dual-BERT design enhances robustness, contextual awareness, and generalization, making the model highly effective for transforming inconsistent Hausa UGC into standardized text suitable for downstream NLP applications. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieved an Exact Match Accuracy of 83.99%, BLEU score of 0.7534, WER of 12.02%, and CER of 7.03%, outperforming the evaluated baseline models across all reported metrics. Qualitative analysis further shows that the model effectively normalizes abbreviations, phonetic spellings, character elongations, and many Hausa-English code-mixed expressions, while insertion and deletion errors remain comparatively more challenging. The primary contributions of this work are (i) the construction of a manually annotated parallel corpus for Hausa user-generated text normalization, (ii) the development of a Dual-BERT adversarial framework for context-aware normalization in a low-resource setting, and (iii) a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach for improving the quality of Hausa user-generated text and supporting downstream NLP applications.

glossary.explanation_id: Proses mengubah teks non-standar atau informal menjadi bentuk standar yang sesuai untuk aplikasi hilir.
Arsitektur *deep learning* di mana dua jaringan berkompetisi, yaitu generator yang membuat data tiruan dan diskriminator yang mendeteksi keaslian data tersebut.
Algoritma tokenisasi yang memecah kata menjadi unit subkata untuk menangani kosakata di luar kamus secara efektif.
Metrik evaluasi yang mengukur persentase prediksi yang persis sama dengan referensi emas.
Fenomena pencampuran dua bahasa atau lebih dalam satu ucapan atau kalimat yang sama.

background.en: Text normalization is a crucial preprocessing task in natural language processing that transforms noisy, informal texts into standardized forms for downstream applications such as machine translation and sentiment analysis. User-generated content from social media platforms frequently contains irregularities like abbreviations, phonetic spellings, code-switching, and orthographic inconsistencies. These issues present significant challenges for low-resource languages such as Hausa, which suffer from limited annotated corpora and contextual ambiguities. Existing rule-based and statistical methods struggle with spelling variations and code-mixing, while standard neural networks lack sufficient specialized parallel resources for efficient training.
background.id: Normalisasi teks adalah tugas prapemrosesan krusial dalam pemrosesan bahasa alami yang mengubah teks bising dan informal menjadi bentuk standar untuk aplikasi hilir seperti terjemahan mesin dan analisis sentimen. Konten buatan pengguna dari platform media sosial sering kali mengandung ketidakteraturan seperti singkatan, ejaan fonetik, alih kode, dan inkonsistensi ortografis. Masalah ini menghadirkan tantangan besar bagi bahasa berikonomi rendah seperti Hausa, yang kekurangan korpus beranotasi dan memiliki ambiguitas kontekstual. Metode berbasis aturan dan statistik yang ada kesulitan menghadapi variasi ejaan dan pencampuran kode, sementara jaringan saraf tiruan standar kekurangan sumber daya paralel khusus yang memadai untuk pelatihan yang efisien.

contributions.en: The primary contributions of this work include the construction of a manually annotated parallel corpus for Hausa user-generated text normalization comprising tweets and WhatsApp messages. Additionally, the authors develop a novel Dual-BERT adversarial framework tailored for context-aware normalization in a low-resource setting, utilizing two parallel BERT encoders within a generator-discriminator architecture. Finally, a comprehensive evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving the quality of Hausa user-generated text and supporting downstream natural language processing applications.
contributions.id: Kontribusi utama dari karya ini mencakup pembangunan korpus paralel beranotasi manual untuk normalisasi teks buatan pengguna bahasa Hausa yang terdiri dari twit dan pesan WhatsApp. Selain itu, para penulis mengembangkan kerangka kerja *adversarial* Dual-BERT baru yang dirancang khusus untuk normalisasi sadar konteks pada pengaturan *low-resource*, dengan memanfaatkan dua penyandi BERT paralel dalam arsitektur generator-diskriminator. Terakhir, evaluasi komprehensif menunjukkan keefektifan pendekatan yang diusulkan dalam meningkatkan kualitas teks buatan pengguna bahasa Hausa dan mendukung aplikasi pemrosesan bahasa alami hilir.

future_work.en: Future work will focus on expanding the corpus to include additional social media platforms and broader dialectal coverage, investigating larger multilingual and language-specific pretrained language models, conducting comprehensive ablation studies, and evaluating the framework across additional downstream natural language processing tasks.
future_work.id: PenyemPURNAan di masa mendatang akan berfokus pada perluasan korpus untuk mencakup platform media sosial tambahan dan cakupan dialek yang lebih luas, investigasi model bahasa pratertatih multilingual dan spesifik bahasa yang lebih besar, pelaksanaan studi ablasi yang komprehensif, serta evaluasi kerangka kerja pada tugas pemrosesan bahasa alami hilir tambahan.

method.en: The study develops a Dual-BERT adversarial network consisting of a generator and a discriminator. The generator employs a pretrained multilingual BERT encoder to process unnormalized inputs, followed by a linear transformation layer using softmax to predict normalized subword tokens in parallel based on WordPiece tokenization. The discriminator functions as a binary classifier utilizing another BERT encoder and a classification head to distinguish between real normalized sentences and generator-produced outputs. Both networks are trained in an adversarial framework using the AdamW optimizer with label smoothing and gradient clipping to stabilize training and ensure end-to-end differentiability.
method.id: Studi ini mengembangkan jaringan *adversarial* Dual-BERT yang terdiri dari generator dan diskriminator. Generator menggunakan penyandi BERT multilingual pratertatih untuk memproses masukan yang belum dinormalisasi, diikuti oleh lapisan transformasi linier menggunakan *softmax* untuk memprediksi token subkata yang dinormalisasi secara paralel berdasarkan tokenisasi WordPiece. Diskriminator berfungsi sebagai pengklasifikasi biner yang memanfaatkan penyandi BERT lain dan kepala klasifikasi untuk membedakan kalimat dinormalisasi asli dari keluaran buatan generator. Kedua jaringan dilatih dalam kerangka kerja *adversarial* menggunakan pengoptimasi AdamW dengan *label smoothing* dan *gradient clipping* untuk menstabilkan pelatihan serta memastikan diferensiabilitas ujung-ke-ujung.

related_work.en: Early research in text normalization primarily relied on dictionary-based and rule-based approaches, which struggle to generalize to unseen abbreviations, evolving social media vocabulary, or code-mixed expressions. Subsequent statistical methods utilized string-level, phonetic, and contextual similarity measures to match out-of-vocabulary terms, yet still depended on handcrafted features. Recent advancements introduced neural network models such as sequence-to-sequence encoders and decoders, recurrent neural networks, and attention mechanisms to automatically learn patterns from data. However, existing Hausa normalization studies remain limited to basic dictionary and spelling correction approaches without fully exploiting contextual transformer representations combined with adversarial learning.
related_work.id: Penelitian awal dalam normalisasi teks terutama mengandalkan pendekatan berbasis kamus dan aturan, yang kesulitan melakukan generalisasi terhadap singkatan baru, kosakata media sosial yang berkembang, atau ekspresi campur kode. Metode statistik selanjutnya menggunakan ukuran kemiripan tingkat string, fonetik, dan kontekstual untuk mencocokkan istilah di luar kosakata, namun masih bergantung pada fitur buatan tangan. Kemajuan terkini memperkenalkan model jaringan saraf tiruan seperti penyandi dan penerjemah *sequence-to-sequence*, jaringan saraf berulang, dan mekanisme *attention* untuk mempelajari pola dari data secara otomatis. Kendati demikian, studi normalisasi Hausa yang ada masih terbatas pada pendekatan kamus dasar dan koreksi ejaan tanpa mengeksploitasi representasi *transformer* kontekstual yang dikombinasikan dengan *adversarial learning* secara penuh.

results.en: The proposed Dual-BERT adversarial model achieved an exact match accuracy of 83.99%, a BLEU score of 0.7534, a word error rate of 12.02%, and a character error rate of 7.03%, outperforming baseline models including Transformer Seq2Seq, mBERT, and mT5 across all metrics. Qualitative analysis indicates that the model excels at normalizing abbreviations, phonetic spellings, character elongations, and code-mixed expressions, though insertion and deletion errors remain relatively challenging.
results.id: Model *adversarial* Dual-BERT yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi *exact match* sebesar 83,99%, skor BLEU 0.7534, tingkat kesalahan kata (*WER*) 12,02%, dan tingkat kesalahan karakter (*CER*) 7,03%, mengungguli model *baseline* termasuk Transformer Seq2Seq, mBERT, and mT5 pada semua metrik. Analisis kualitatif menunjukkan bahwa model ini unggul dalam menormalisasi singkatan, ejaan fonetik, pemanjangan karakter, dan ekspresi campur kode, meskipun kesalahan penambahan dan penghapusan masih relatif menantang.

tldr.en: This paper proposes a Dual-BERT adversarial network for normalizing user-generated Hausa text into its standard form. Experiments demonstrate that the model significantly outperforms baseline approaches in exact match accuracy, BLEU, WER, and CER.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengusulkan sebuah *adversarial network* berbasis Dual-BERT untuk menormalisasi teks Hausa buatan pengguna ke dalam bentuk standarnya. Eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa model ini mengungguli pendekatan *baseline* secara signifikan dalam metrik akurasi *exact match*, *BLEU*, *WER*, dan *CER*.

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1905680.title: Dual-BERT adversarial learning for Hausa user-generated text normalization

doi:10.3390/a19090795.abstract: OCR for low-resource languages is still held back by the same small number of issues: too little labeled image-text data, too few benchmarks, and thin language-specific tooling. Kurdish Sorani is a particularly awkward case. It is written in a modified Arabic script, runs right to left, and has orthographic habits that standard Arabic OCR engines handle poorly. This paper describes a transformer OCR system for Sorani trained almost entirely on synthetic data, meaning line images rendered on the fly from a text corpus rather than manually transcribed scans. The pipeline has three parts: corpus-driven line synthesis, a deterministic script-aware normalization step based on character-level transliteration, and a TrOCR encoder–decoder recognizer. Text lines are rendered with randomly sampled fonts and sizes, then passed through stochastic augmentation to mimic realistic distortions. The system is evaluated twice. On an in-distribution synthetic set of 200 rendered lines, the best model reaches a character error rate of 0.0434, a word error rate of 0.1246, and 64.0% exact matches. More importantly, on a real-world test set of 19 scanned Kurdish documents (467 lines, 28,468 characters) processed end-to-end through detection and recognition, it reaches a character error rate of 0.0305 and a word error rate of 0.1770, beating both Arabic and Kurdish Tesseract baselines and an existing Kurdish TrOCR model while being considerably smaller than the latter. A controlled ablation, in which eight variants are trained under one shared budget and scored on identical images, then isolates what each design choice contributes. The label space is the largest design effect, and the reason is concrete: the decoder’s pre-trained tokenizer has no representation for seven common Sorani graphemes, which cover 14.7% of the corpus and place a floor under any model trained on native-script labels. Corpus size dominates overall and behaves as a threshold, font diversity helps with diminishing returns, and stochastic augmentation buys robustness at a small cost in in-distribution accuracy. Aligning detected lines against the transcribed ones further shows that line detection contributes under 1% of the reported character error on this material. The broader point, at least for Sorani, is that the synthetic training data and the label space in which the model predicts have to be designed together: a compact recognizer built that way outperforms a substantially larger released Kurdish model on genuine document images.

glossary.explanation_id: TrOCR adalah model *transformer* untuk tugas *optical character recognition* yang menggabungkan *image encoder* dan *text decoder*.
Character error rate adalah metrik evaluasi yang mengukur persentase kesalahan karakter antara teks prediksi dan teks referensi.
Word error rate adalah metrik evaluasi yang menghitung jumlah minimum operasi penyuntingan yang diperlukan untuk mengubah kata-kata prediksi menjadi kata-kata acuan.
Stochastic augmentation adalah teknik penambahan variasi acak pada data pelatihan untuk meningkatkan ketahanan model.
Ablation adalah metode analisis dengan menghapus atau mengubah komponen tertentu dari model secara sistematis untuk memahami kontribusinya.
Tokenizer adalah komponen yang memecah teks masukan menjadi unit-unit yang lebih kecil seperti kata atau subkata untuk diproses oleh model.
Transliteration adalah proses pengalihan aksara dari satu sistem tulisan ke sistem tulisan lainnya.

background.en:
Optical character recognition for low-resource languages is hindered by a scarcity of labeled image-text data, a lack of benchmarks, and limited language-specific tooling. Kurdish Sorani represents a particularly challenging case due to its modified Arabic script, right-to-left writing direction, and orthographic characteristics that standard Arabic engines process poorly.

Addressing these obstacles requires overcoming data scarcity and script-specific normalization issues to build robust text recognition systems for low-resource writing systems without relying heavily on expensive manual transcription.
background.id:
Pengenalan karakter optik untuk bahasa *low-resource* terkendala oleh kelangkaan data *image-text* beranotasi, kurangnya *benchmark*, dan terbatasnya perkakas spesifik bahasa. Bahasa Kurdish Sorani merepresentasikan kasus yang sangat menantang karena skrip Arab yang dimodifikasi, arah penulisan dari kanan ke kiri, dan karakteristik ortografis yang diproses secara buruk oleh mesin standar Arab.

Mengatasi hambatan tersebut menuntut penyelesaian masalah kelangkaan data dan normalisasi spesifik skrip untuk membangun sistem pengenalan teks yang tangguh pada sistem penulisan *low-resource* tanpa sangat bergantung pada transkripsi manual yang mahal.

contributions.en:
The primary contribution is a compact, transformer-based OCR pipeline for Kurdish Sorani trained almost entirely on synthetic data rendered on the fly from a text corpus. Additional novel aspects include a deterministic script-aware normalization step using character-level transliteration and a TrOCR encoder-decoder recognizer.

Further novelty stems from a controlled ablation study investigating eight design variants, which isolates the specific contributions of label space, corpus size, font diversity, and stochastic augmentation.
contributions.id:
Kontribusi utamanya adalah *pipeline* OCR berbasis *transformer* yang ringkas untuk bahasa Kurdish Sorani yang dilatih hampir sepenuhnya pada data sintetis yang dirender secara langsung (*on the fly*) dari korpus teks. Aspek kebaruan tambahan mencakup langkah normalisasi deterministik yang sadar skrip menggunakan transliterasi tingkat karakter serta *recognizer* *encoder-decoder* *TrOCR*.

Kebaruan lebih lanjut berasal dari studi ablasi terkontrol yang menyelidiki delapan varian desain, yang mengisolasi kontribusi spesifik dari ruang *label*, ukuran korpus, keragaman *font*, dan *stochastic augmentation*.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan secara rinci.

method.en:
The pipeline consists of corpus-driven line synthesis, a deterministic script-aware normalization step based on character-level transliteration, and a TrOCR encoder-decoder recognizer. Text lines are rendered dynamically using randomly sampled fonts and sizes, followed by stochastic augmentation to introduce realistic distortions.

The system is evaluated on both an in-distribution synthetic set of 200 rendered lines and a real-world test set of 19 scanned Kurdish documents comprising 467 lines and 28,468 characters processed end-to-end through detection and recognition.
method.id:
Pipeline tersebut terdiri atas sintesis baris berbasis korpus, langkah normalisasi deterministik yang sadar skrip berdasarkan transliterasi tingkat karakter, dan *recognizer* *encoder-decoder* *TrOCR*. Baris teks dirender secara dinamis menggunakan *font* dan ukuran yang diambil secara acak (*randomly sampled*), diikuti oleh *stochastic augmentation* untuk memperkenalkan distorsi yang realistis.

Sistem dievaluasi pada set sintetis *in-distribution* sebanyak 200 baris terender dan set uji dunia nyata dari 19 dokumen pindaian Kurdi yang mencakup 467 baris dan 28.468 karakter yang diproses secara *end-to-end* melalui deteksi dan pengenalan.

related_work.en:
The paper compares its approach against Arabic and Kurdish Tesseract baselines as well as an existing Kurdish TrOCR model. The authors note that the existing Kurdish TrOCR model is substantially larger than their proposed system and suffers from limitations related to its pre-trained label space and tokenizer representations.

Prior studies and systems struggle with Sorani because standard Arabic OCR engines fail to handle its unique orthographic habits, and existing large models lack appropriate representations for essential language-specific graphemes.
related_work.id:
Makalah ini membandingkan pendekatannya terhadap *baseline* Tesseract bahasa Arab dan Kurdi serta model *TrOCR* bahasa Kurdi yang sudah ada. Penulis mencatat bahwa model *TrOCR* bahasa Kurdi yang ada berukuran jauh lebih besar daripada sistem yang diusulkan dan mengalami keterbatasan yang berkaitan dengan ruang *label* prasasti (*pre-trained*) serta representasi *tokenizer*.

Studi dan sistem sebelumnya mengalami kesulitan dengan bahasa Sorani karena mesin OCR standar Arab gagal menangani kebiasaan ortografisnya yang unik, dan model besar yang ada tidak memiliki representasi yang tepat untuk grafem spesifik bahasa yang esensial.

results.en:
On the synthetic test set, the best model achieves a character error rate of 0.0434, a word error rate of 0.1246, and 64.0 percent exact matches. On the real-world scanned document test set, the system reaches a character error rate of 0.0305 and a word error rate of 0.1770, outperforming Arabic and Kurdish Tesseract baselines as well as a larger existing Kurdish TrOCR model.

Controlled ablations reveal that the label space is the most impactful design choice because the pre-trained tokenizer lacks representations for seven common Sorani graphemes covering 14.7 percent of the corpus. Corpus size acts as a threshold, font diversity exhibits diminishing returns, stochastic augmentation improves robustness with a minor cost to in-distribution accuracy, and line detection contributes less than 1 percent of the character error.
results.id:
Pada set uji sintetis, model terbaik mencapai tingkat kesalahan karakter sebesar 0,0434, tingkat kesalahan kata sebesar 0,1246, dan *exact match* sebesar 64,0 persen. Pada set uji dokumen pindaian dunia nyata, sistem mencapai tingkat kesalahan karakter sebesar 0,0305 dan tingkat kesalahan kata sebesar 0,1770, mengungguli *baseline* Tesseract bahasa Arab dan Kurdi serta model *TrOCR* Kurdi eksisting yang lebih besar.

Ablasi terkontrol menunjukkan bahwa ruang *label* adalah pilihan desain yang paling berdampak karena *tokenizer* prasasti tidak memiliki representasi untuk tujuh grafem umum Sorani yang mencakup 14,7 persen dari korpus. Ukuran korpus bertindak sebagai ambang batas (*threshold*), keragaman *font* menunjukkan hasil yang semakin berkurang (*diminishing returns*), *stochastic augmentation* meningkatkan ketahanan dengan biaya kecil pada akurasi *in-distribution*, dan deteksi baris menyumbang kurang dari 1 persen dari kesalahan karakter.

tldr.en: This paper presents a transformer OCR system for Kurdish Sorani trained almost entirely on synthetic data. The approach achieves lower error rates than existing models on real-world scanned documents.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyajikan sistem *transformer* OCR untuk bahasa Kurdish Sorani yang dilatih hampir sepenuhnya menggunakan data sintetis. Pendekatan tersebut mencapai tingkat kesalahan yang lebih rendah daripada model-model yang ada pada dokumen pindaian dunia nyata.

doi:10.3390/a19090795.title: Synthetic Data-Driven Transformer OCR for Kurdish Sorani via Dynamic Line Generation and Script-Aware Normalization

doi:10.3390/app16157505.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have advanced machine translation, but their quality on low-resource language pairs remains uneven and is typically assessed with automatic metrics alone. This study examines how prompting strategy and source-text type jointly affect LLM translation quality for the low-resource Chinese–Vietnamese pair and whether automatic and human assessments agree. Using a 2 × 3 mixed factorial design, we compared an English-mediated pivot strategy with a direct strategy across informative, expressive, and operative texts, evaluating 60 ChatGPT translations with COMET and with 15 bilingual readers who rated adequacy, fluency, faithfulness, trustworthiness, willingness to use, and need for revision. On COMET, pivoting significantly improved overall quality (p < 0.001), text type was the dominant factor (η2 = 0.91; informative > operative > expressive), and strategy interacted with text type, with the largest pivot gain for expressive texts. Human ratings reproduced this ordering but diverged sharply for expressive texts: although COMET favoured the pivot output, readers reported that pivoting raised fluency yet substantially reduced faithfulness (4.10 → 1.77 on a 7-point scale) and were unwilling to accept it. These results show that the value of a prompting strategy is text-type-dependent and that fluent LLM output is not necessarily faithful, underscoring the need to pair automatic metrics with human evaluation when benchmarking low-resource translation.
doi:10.3390/app16157505.title: Effects of Pivot Prompting and Text Type on LLM Translation Quality for the Low-Resource Chinese–Vietnamese Pair: Evidence from COMET and Human Evaluation

doi:10.3390/bdcc10080278.abstract: Small Language Models (SLMs) enable efficient deployment, but their limited parameter count constrains factual knowledge, particularly in low-resource languages like Kazakh. Integrating live web search can address this limitation, though its effectiveness is difficult to measure due to sparse in-language web indices and answer leakage during benchmarking. In this study, we systematically compare zero-shot parametric generation, in-language retrieval, and cross-lingual (translate-then-retrieve) web search using three 4B-parameter SLMs in both reasoning and non-reasoning modes. To evaluate factuality without search-engine leakage, we introduce machine-translated Kazakh versions of the FreshQA and DefAn benchmarks, and use GPQA as a Google-proof adversarial control. We also assess robustness across three prompt complexities, from simple JSON constraints to adversarial warnings that instruct the model to treat potentially unreliable context with caution. Finally, we propose a training-free, self-aware router that uses majority voting over repeated self-verification decisions to determine when to answer parametrically, when to search the web, and when to escalate to a more capable cloud model. Our results show that cross-lingual retrieval substantially outperforms in-language search on global factuality tasks, nearly doubling accuracy on FreshQA, while direct in-language search remains preferable for localized cultural queries. The choice of retrieval language depends on the task and does not always favor English. Additionally, cross-lingual retrieval is not consistently superior, because the best option depends on where relevant information is indexed. Pareto analysis indicates that cross-lingual search is on or near the optimal accuracy–latency frontier, adding minimal overhead compared to direct search. The router identifies which query types warrant retrieval, and as a system it tracks or exceeds always-search accuracy while issuing fewer searches and approaching the always-cloud ceiling at a fraction of its cost; per-query discrimination within a task family is weaker, which we quantify explicitly. Overall, this work offers a framework for optimizing and accurately measuring cross-lingual RAG pipelines in low-resource settings.
doi:10.3390/bdcc10080278.title: Translate, Search, or Answer: Cost-Aware Cross-Lingual Retrieval for Kazakh Small Language Models

doi:10.3390/computers15090627.abstract: Multilingual code-switched language identification remains a challenging task due to frequent language alternation, lexical ambiguity, and the limited availability of annotated corpora for low-resource languages. While transformer-based language models have demonstrated strong performance, their computational complexity motivates the exploration of more efficient neuromorphic approaches. This study proposes an optimized Spiking Neural Network (SNN) framework for multilingual code-switched language identification using spike-based neural computation. Text data are preprocessed and represented using Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) feature vectors, which are transformed into temporal spike trains through a rate-coding mechanism over a fixed simulation window. The encoded spike sequences are processed by a feedforward SNN employing Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons. Hyperparameters are optimized using Optuna to improve classification performance. The proposed model is evaluated on a balanced multilingual code-switched dataset and compared with classical machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest, as well as deep learning and transformer-based models, including BiLSTM, mBERT, AfroXLMR, and XLM-RoBERTa. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized SNN achieves an overall classification accuracy of 81%, outperforming the baseline SNN while remaining competitive with several state-of-the-art neural models. Statistical validation using the Friedman and Nemenyi tests confirms significant performance differences among the evaluated classifiers while demonstrating that the optimized SNN performs competitively against several strong baselines. Although transformer models achieve the highest overall accuracy, the proposed SNN offers a computationally efficient neuromorphic alternative that combines temporal spike processing with stable learning behaviour for multilingual code-switched language identification. These findings demonstrate the potential of spike-based neural computing for low-resource multilingual natural language processing and provide a reproducible foundation for future neuromorphic language identification research.

glossary.explanation_id: Arsitektur *neural network* tiruan yang menggunakan *spike* diskrit untuk pemrosesan informasi dan komunikasi antar neuron.
Fenomena penggunaan dua bahasa atau lebih secara bergantian dalam satu percakapan atau teks.
Metode pembobotan statistik yang mengukur seberapa penting suatu kata dalam dokumen relatif terhadap korpus.
Mekanisme pengodean informasi ke dalam frekuensi kemunculan *spike* dalam *Spiking Neural Network*.
Model neuron biologis sederhana yang mengakumulasi sinyal masukan hingga ambang batas tertentu tercapai untuk memicu *spike*.
Parameter eksternal yang nilainya ditetapkan sebelum proses pembelajaran *model* dimulai.
Pendekatan komputasi yang meniru struktur dan fungsi sistem saraf biologis.

background.en: Multilingual code-switched language identification remains a challenging task due to frequent language alternation, lexical ambiguity, and the limited availability of annotated corpora for low-resource languages. Although transformer-based language models have demonstrated strong performance, their high computational complexity motivates the exploration of more efficient neuromorphic alternatives.
background.id: Identifikasi bahasa pada teks *code-switched* multilingual tetap menjadi tugas yang menantang karena pergantian bahasa yang sering, ambiguitas leksikal, dan terbatasnya ketersediaan korpus beranotasi untuk bahasa *low-resource*. Meskipun *model bahasa* berbasis *transformer* telah menunjukkan performa yang kuat, kompleksitas komputasinya yang tinggi memotivasi eksplorasi alternatif *neuromorphic* yang lebih efisien.

contributions.en: This study proposes an optimized Spiking Neural Network framework for multilingual code-switched language identification using spike-based neural computation. The contributions include combining temporal spike processing with stable learning behavior, optimizing hyperparameters using Optuna, and providing a reproducible foundation for future neuromorphic language identification research.
contributions.id: Studi ini mengusulkan *framework* *Spiking Neural Network* yang dioptimalkan untuk identifikasi bahasa pada teks *code-switched* multilingual menggunakan komputasi saraf berbasis *spike*. Kontribusinya meliputi penggabungan pemrosesan *spike* temporal dengan perilaku pembelajaran yang stabil, pengoptimalan *hyperparameter* menggunakan Optuna, dan penyediaan fondasi yang dapat direproduksi untuk riset identifikasi bahasa *neuromorphic* di masa depan.

future_work.en: The paper does not discuss future work in detail, but notes that the findings provide a reproducible foundation for future neuromorphic language identification research.
future_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan masa depan secara rinci, namun mencatat bahwa temuan-temuan tersebut memberikan fondasi yang dapat direproduksi untuk riset identifikasi bahasa *neuromorphic* di masa depan.

method.en: Text data are preprocessed and represented using TF-IDF feature vectors, which are transformed into temporal spike trains through a rate-coding mechanism over a fixed simulation window. The encoded spike sequences are processed by a feedforward Spiking Neural Network employing Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons, with hyperparameters optimized using Optuna. The model is evaluated on a balanced multilingual code-switched dataset and validated using the Friedman and Nemenyi statistical tests.

Sekuens *spike* yang dikodekan diproses oleh *feedforward* *Spiking Neural Network* yang menggunakan neuron *Leaky Integrate-and-Fire*, dengan *hyperparameter* yang dioptimalkan menggunakan Optuna. Model ini dievaluasi pada *dataset* *code-switched* multilingual yang seimbang dan divalidasi menggunakan uji statistik Friedman dan Nemenyi.

related_work.en: The authors compare their proposed Spiking Neural Network with classical machine learning models including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. They also compare it against deep learning and transformer-based models including BiLSTM, mBERT, AfroXLMR, and XLM-RoBERTa.
related_work.id: Para penulis membandingkan *Spiking Neural Network* yang mereka usulkan dengan model *machine learning* klasik termasuk *Logistic Regression*, *Support Vector Machine*, dan *Random Forest*. Mereka juga membandingkannya dengan model *deep learning* dan berbasis *transformer* termasuk *BiLSTM*, *mBERT*, *AfroXLMR*, and *XLM-RoBERTa*.

results.en: Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized Spiking Neural Network achieves an overall classification accuracy of 81 percent, outperforming the baseline Spiking Neural Network while remaining competitive with several state-of-the-art neural models. Statistical validation confirms significant performance differences among the evaluated classifiers.
