Validasi statistik mengonfirmasi adanya perbedaan performa yang signifikan di antara pengklasifikasi yang dievaluasi.

tldr.en: This paper proposes an optimized Spiking Neural Network framework for multilingual code-switched language identification. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an overall classification accuracy of 81 percent, outperforming baseline models and remaining competitive with transformer-based approaches.
tldr.id: Studi ini mengusulkan *framework* *Spiking Neural Network* yang dioptimalkan untuk identifikasi bahasa pada teks *code-switched* multilingual. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa model yang diusulkan mencapai akurasi klasifikasi keseluruhan sebesar 81 persen, mengungguli model *baseline* dan tetap kompetitif dengan pendekatan berbasis *transformer*.

doi:10.3390/computers15090627.title: Neuromorphic-Inspired Language Identification for Low-Resource Code-Switched Texts Using Spiking Neural Networks

doi:10.3390/data11080196.abstract: Automatic extraction of genealogical information from historical archival-genealogical documents in Uzbek is an understudied problem for low-resource languages. Multi-layer NLP benchmarks are not sufficient to automatically identify individuals, family relationships, dates, place names, and archival identifiers in such texts. Also, the same people are mentioned in various forms: full name, pronoun (18.8%), initial, surname-name order, indirect expression (9.4%), and title. Existing NER and relation extraction corpora are mainly focused on high-resource languages or general domain texts and do not sufficiently cover the FAMILY_ROLE signals, historical spelling variants, and fond–opis–delos identifiers specific to Uzbek archival-genealogical texts. Proposed resource: We present the ArchiveGene Corpus, a controlled, fully synthetic, and reproducible five-layer resource consisting of 1000 Uzbek archival-genealogical-style documents, divided into 700 training, 150 validation, and 150 test documents. The corpus contains 8366 named entities, 10,625 person mentions, 2000 coreference chains, and 1000 genealogical relation triples. The dataset was generated using a deterministic template-based pipeline and a lexicon of Uzbek names, and is fully reproducible. Inter-annotator agreement values were 0.847 for NER, 0.793 for coreference, and 0.821 for RE, according to Cohen’s κ. Comparative results are presented with four baseline models (rule-based, BiLSTM-CRF, mBERT, and XLM-RoBERTa). The dataset is openly hosted on the Zenodo platform under the CC BY 4.0 license; concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20670360, v1.1.1 version DOI: 10.5281/zenodo. 21429998. Scientific significance: To the best of our knowledge, ArchiveGene is among the first openly released, controlled synthetic resources for Uzbek that integrates named-entity recognition, person-mention detection, coreference resolution, genealogical relation extraction, and final tuple generation within a single annotation framework. The baseline analysis provides three main conclusions: (1) on the clean synthetic test set, the transformer models already reach 100.00 Micro-F1 for NER and 100.00 Macro-F1 for coreference-aware relation extraction, so coreference aggregation adds little on synthetic data (+2.25 for mBERT and +0.04 for XLM-RoBERTa) but its contribution is expected to grow on real archival text; (2) the rule-based and heuristic baselines lag far behind (Macro-F1 50.28 and 70.73) and fail entirely on spouse_of, showing the limits of lexical rules; and (3) a zero-shot evaluation on a real-document pilot reduces NER Micro-F1 from 100.00 to 22.17, indicating that the synthetic corpus is trivially learnable and that real-archival validation is essential.
doi:10.3390/data11080196.title: The ArchiveGene Corpus: A Synthetic Multi-Layer Benchmark for Genealogical Information Extraction from Uzbek Historical Archival Texts

doi:10.3390/data11090217.abstract: The availability of large, structured legal datasets is essential for advancing legal natural language processing, information retrieval, and the development of reliable language technologies. However, such resources remain scarce for Kazakh, a morphologically rich and comparatively low-resource language, limiting the development and evaluation of domain-specific NLP methods. This data descriptor presents KazakhLawCorpus, a curated corpus of 215,889 document-level legislative metadata records from the Republic of Kazakhstan. The dataset was derived from a PostgreSQL export containing 223,245 source records and constructed through Kazakh-language field selection, essential-field filtering, source-preserving normalization, schema reconstruction, and systematic quality validation, resulting in a retention rate of 96.705%. The final release comprises 25 fields covering document identifiers, temporal attributes, legal status, registry information, Kazakh-language titles and descriptions, legal and institutional categories, geographical information, and source URLs. The records cover legislative acts adopted between 30 October 1947 and 20 July 2026. Quality-control procedures confirmed unique law_id values, complete title and description fields, and parseable adoption dates, while 4635 records with potential source-level or historical anomalies were retained and transparently documented through diagnostic flags. KazakhLawCorpus provides a large-scale, traceable resource for metadata-based legal information retrieval, document classification, temporal and institutional analysis, provenance tracking, and the development of downstream Kazakh legal NLP resources.
doi:10.3390/data11090217.title: KazakhLawCorpus: A Large-Scale Metadata Corpus for Kazakh Legislation

doi:10.3390/economies14090419.abstract: This study explores the drivers of income inequality using crude oil prices, consumer prices, economic development, trade openness, unemployment, and human capital as predictors. Despite a lot of research conducted on income inequality, there have been very few studies capable of simultaneously analysing the influence of energy prices, macroeconomic conditions, trade openness, conditions in the labour market, and human capital, as well as accounting for the dynamic persistence and potential endogeneity of inequality across countries. To fill this research gap, based on a panel of 230 observations, analyses are run using pooled ordinary least squares, as well as fixed and random effects derived from model-selection tests that favour the random effects specification. An analysis using a dynamic panel data model was also carried out in this study. The empirical results show that crude oil prices, trade openness, and unemployment are all positively correlated with income inequality and that GDP per capita and human capital have a significant deterrent effect on the expansion of income inequality. With the random effects model, a US$1 increase in crude oil prices increases the Gini index by 0.0186 points; meanwhile, one-percentage-point increases in trade openness and unemployment contribute to increases in inequality of 0.0142 points and 0.722 points, respectively. On the other hand, a US$1000 increase in GDP per capita lowers the Gini index by about 0.0699 points, and an improvement of 0.1 point in human capital decreases inequality by approximately 1.497 points. Controlling for country-specific effects does little to show an association with consumer prices. The model accounts for 43.11 per cent of the variation in income inequality. The findings show that inclusive growth strategies, investment in human capital and labour-market policies are evidently pivotal to addressing inequality fostered by economic transformation and energy-price volatility.
doi:10.3390/economies14090419.title: The Influence of Oil Prices on Income Inequality in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations

doi:10.3390/electronics15173856.abstract: Real-time event detection from social media has become increasingly important for emergency response, public safety, and situational awareness. However, accurately identifying emerging events from Thai social media remains challenging because Thai is a low-resource language without explicit word boundaries, while social media text is often characterized by informal writing, spelling variations, and noisy user-generated content. This paper proposes an entity-centric real-time event detection framework for Thai social media that employs a Multi-Granularity Thai Character Cluster (TCC)-Aware Named Entity Recognition (NER) model as its core information extraction component. The proposed NER architecture integrates contextual word embeddings, character-level representations, Thai Character Cluster features, and Part-of-Speech embeddings through an attention-based feature fusion mechanism to improve entity recognition under noisy conditions. Recognized entities are subsequently used as semantic anchors for event construction, clustering, temporal trend analysis, event ranking, and alert generation within a unified streaming framework. Event discovery combines Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) and Exponential Moving Average (EMA)-based temporal analysis to identify emerging events in real time. Experiments conducted on a large-scale Thai social media corpus demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an F1-score of 94.14% for named entity recognition and 92.2% for downstream event detection, outperforming representative baseline methods. Additional ablation studies, qualitative error analysis, and statistical significance tests confirm the effectiveness of the proposed multi-granularity representation. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective solution for real-time event monitoring in low-resource language environments.
doi:10.3390/electronics15173856.title: An Entity-Centric Real-Time Event Detection Framework for Thai Social Media Using Multi-Granularity TCC-Aware Named Entity Recognition

doi:10.3390/info17080753.abstract: Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging is a foundational task in Natural Language Processing (NLP), yet it remains challenging for low-resource and morphologically rich languages such as Amazigh. This paper proposes a hybrid ensemble framework for Amazigh POS tagging that integrates three complementary models: a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network (BiLSTM), a Conditional Random Field model (CRF), and a rule-based morphological analyzer (RBMA). Rather than treating prior results obtained on different corpora and tag inventories as directly comparable, the study evaluates all proposed components under a common 54-tag experimental setting based on the publicly available Amazigh Linguistic Dataset. Three ensemble strategies are examined: majority voting, validation-weighted voting, and logistic-regression stacking. An additional late-fusion ablation applies hard and soft RBMA constraints to CRF and Stacking outputs; hard masking degrades performance substantially, whereas soft masking is more robust but remains below unconstrained decoding. The best micro-level performance is obtained by the stacking ensemble, which reaches 98.51% Micro-F1/accuracy, whereas the boosting-like weighted ensemble obtains the strongest Macro-F1 among the ensemble variants, reaching 74.24%. These results show that hybrid ensemble methods can improve token-level accuracy in low-resource POS tagging, while also revealing a trade-off between frequent-tag accuracy and rare-tag robustness. The findings highlight the usefulness of combining neural, probabilistic, and rule-based information for Amazigh POS tagging, and point to class-balanced meta-learning and character/subword representations as important directions for improving rare and out-of-vocabulary categories.
doi:10.3390/info17080753.title: Ensemble-Based Approach for Amazigh POS Tagging: Leveraging Multiple Models for Enhanced Performance in Low-Resource Language Processing

doi:10.3390/info17090921.abstract: Fine-tuning is often treated as a prerequisite for deploying large language models in low-resource languages, yet its value for recent open-weight models is unclear. We evaluate eleven checkpoints of 7–14 billion parameters before and after Low-Rank Adaptation on 5000 human-curated Kazakh instruction–response pairs. Evaluation is performed on the Kazakh splits of KazMMLU, ARC, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and GSM8K, with Russian GSM8K as a higher-resource comparison. Our central finding is a language asymmetry: the same Kazakh-trained adapters improved Russian GSM8K more than the Kazakh GSM8K they targeted. Excluding one checkpoint that collapsed after fine-tuning by up to 58 percentage points, the remaining ten gained +2.6 percentage points on average on Kazakh (range −6.1 to +13.6) against +6.9 on Russian, significant under a paired signed-rank test. A manual audit of 400 responses identifies a contributing mechanism: Kazakh outputs were more often truncated before a final answer, and correct Kazakh reasoning more often scored wrong by answer extraction, so part of the gap reflects response form, not reasoning. Adaptation produced no meaningful average change on the four multiple-choice benchmarks. GSM8K is the suite’s only free-form task, so generality is untested. These results suggest that low-resource fine-tuning should be evaluated per checkpoint, benchmark, and language rather than being adopted by default.

glossary.explanation_id: Sebuah metode *parameter-efficient fine-tuning* yang melatih matriks rank rendah untuk memperbarui bobot model dengan efisien.
Model bahasa besar yang bobot parameternya dibagikan secara publik untuk penggunaan dan penelitian lebih lanjut.
Keadaan tersimpan dari parameter model pada tahap tertentu selama proses pelatihan atau penyesuaian.
Kondisi di mana suatu bahasa atau domain memiliki ketersediaan data dan sumber daya komputasi yang sangat terbatas.
Kemampuan model untuk melakukan tugas baru tanpa memerlukan contoh pelatihan atau penyesuaian sebelumnya.

background.en: Fine-tuning is commonly regarded as a necessary prerequisite for deploying large language models in low-resource languages. However, the actual value and impact of fine-tuning for recent open-weight models remain unclear, particularly given the potential risks of model degradation and language asymmetry during adaptation.
background.id: Fine-tuning umumnya dianggap sebagai prasyarat yang diperlukan untuk menerapkan large language model pada bahasa low-resource. Namun, nilai aktual dan dampak dari fine-tuning untuk model open-weight terbaru masih belum jelas, terutama mengingat potensi risiko penurunan degradasi model dan asimetri bahasa selama adaptasi.

contributions.en: The paper contributes an evaluation of eleven open-weight models ranging from 7 to 14 billion parameters before and after Low-Rank Adaptation using five thousand human-curated Kazakh instruction-response pairs. It provides empirical insights into the language asymmetry observed between Kazakh and Russian benchmarks.
contributions.id: Makalah ini memberikan kontribusi evaluasi terhadap sebelas model open-weight dengan rentang 7 hingga 14 miliar parameter sebelum dan sesudah Low-Rank Adaptation menggunakan lima ribu pasang instruksi dan respons bahasa Kazakh yang dikurasi oleh manusia. Penelitian ini memberikan wawasan empiris mengenai asimetri bahasa yang diamati antara benchmark bahasa Kazakh dan bahasa Rusia.

future_work.en: The authors note that since GSM8K is the only free-form task in the evaluation suite, the broader generality of these findings remains untested. They suggest that low-resource fine-tuning should be evaluated per checkpoint, benchmark, and language rather than adopted by default.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa karena GSM8K adalah satu-satunya tugas bentuk bebas dalam rangkaian evaluasi, generalisasi yang lebih luas dari temuan ini masih belum diuji. Mereka menyarankan agar fine-tuning bahasa low-resource dievaluasi per checkpoint, benchmark, dan bahasa, alih-alih diadopsi secara bawaan.

method.en: The evaluation uses eleven checkpoints of models with 7 to 14 billion parameters before and after applying Low-Rank Adaptation. The training dataset consists of 5,000 human-curated Kazakh instruction-response pairs. Evaluation is conducted on Kazakh splits of KazMMLU, ARC, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and GSM8K, with Russian GSM8K included as a higher-resource comparison. Additionally, a manual audit of 400 responses is performed to investigate error mechanisms such as output truncation and answer extraction failures.
method.id: Evaluasi ini menggunakan sebelas checkpoint dari model dengan parameter 7 hingga 14 miliar sebelum dan sesudah menerapkan Low-Rank Adaptation. Kumpulan data pelatihan terdiri dari 5.000 pasang instruksi dan respons bahasa Kazakh yang dikurasi oleh manusia. Evaluasi dilakukan pada pembagian bahasa Kazakh dari KazMMLU, ARC, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, dan GSM8K, dengan GSM8K bahasa Rusia yang disertakan sebagai perbandingan sumber daya yang lebih tinggi. Selain itu, audit manual terhadap 400 respons dilakukan untuk menyelidiki mekanisme kesalahan seperti pemotongan keluaran dan kegagalan ekstraksi jawaban.

related_work.en: The paper does not discuss related work in detail.
related_work.id: Makalah ini tidak membahas pekerjaan terkait secara mendetail.

results.en: The central finding is a language asymmetry: Kazakh-trained adapters improved Russian GSM8K performance more than the target Kazakh GSM8K. Excluding one collapsed checkpoint, ten models gained an average of 2.6 percentage points on Kazakh compared to 6.9 on Russian, which is statistically significant under a paired signed-rank test. A manual audit revealed that Kazakh outputs were frequently truncated before a final answer and correct reasoning was often penalized by answer extraction issues. Meanwhile, adaptation produced no meaningful average change on the four multiple-choice benchmarks.
results.id: Temuan utamanya adalah asimetri bahasa: adapter yang dilatih pada bahasa Kazakh meningkatkan performa GSM8K bahasa Rusia lebih besar daripada GSM8K bahasa Kazakh target. Tidak termasuk satu checkpoint yang mengalami keruntuhan, sepuluh model memperoleh rata-rata 2,6 persentase poin pada bahasa Kazakh dibandingkan dengan 6,9 pada bahasa Rusia, yang signifikan secara statistik di bawah uji peringkat bertanda berpasangan. Audit manual mengungkapkan bahwa keluaran bahasa Kazakh sering kali terpotong sebelum jawaban akhir dan penalaran yang benar sering kali disalahkan oleh masalah ekstraksi jawaban. Sementara itu, adaptasi tidak menghasilkan perubahan rata-rata yang berarti pada keempat benchmark pilihan ganda.

tldr.en: This paper evaluates eleven open-weight large language models before and after fine-tuning on Kazakh instruction data across multiple benchmarks. The findings reveal a language asymmetry where adapters improved Russian performance more than Kazakh, and show that low-resource fine-tuning should be evaluated per checkpoint and benchmark rather than adopted by default.
tldr.id: Makalah ini mengevaluasi sebelas *large language model* *open-weight* sebelum dan sesudah *fine-tuning* pada data instruksi bahasa Kazakh di berbagai *benchmark*. Temuan utama mengungkapkan adanya asimetri bahasa di mana *adapter* meningkatkan performa bahasa Rusia lebih besar daripada bahasa Kazakh, serta menunjukkan bahwa *fine-tuning* bahasa *low-resource* harus dievaluasi per *checkpoint* dan *benchmark* dan bukan diadopsi secara bawaan.

doi:10.3390/info17090921.title: When Does Fine-Tuning Matter for a Low-Resource Language? Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs on Kazakh Benchmarks

doi:10.3390/jmse14171658.abstract: A collision avoidance decision-making method that integrates intention recognition with predictive risk perception is proposed to address the uncertainty and dynamic complexity of multi-ship encounters. First, the probabilities of avoidance maneuvers are derived from COLREGs and maritime practice to establish predictive distributions of course alterations. Second, an avoidance-maneuver intention (AMI) confidence coefficient is formulated from evidence fused using Dempster–Shafer (DS) evidence theory to quantify the reliability of the target ship’s maneuver behavior. Third, a predictive risk-perception-based line-of-sight (PRP-LOS) method is developed by introducing a predicted-equivalent virtual ship position into a navigation risk field. Simulation results show that the proposed method accurately infers target-ship AMIs and effectively reduces collision risk while balancing safety and smoothness. These research results provide effective methodological support for improving autonomous decision-making capabilities.
doi:10.3390/jmse14171658.journal_ref: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
doi:10.3390/jmse14171658.title: A Multi-Ship Intelligent Collision Avoidance Decision Method Considering Intention Uncertainty
doi:10.3390/jmse14171658.venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

doi:10.3390/languages11080170.abstract: This paper focuses on historical and new linguistic minorities in educational contexts in Italy. It argues that, despite increasing multilingualism, the Italian educational system remains shaped by a persistent monolingual ideology. Drawing on data from two research projects, La classe plurilingue (2018–2020) and MinEdu—Supporting Minority Languages in Educational Contexts (2023–2026), it examines how different forms of multilingualism, both of which can be framed within a heritage language profile, are managed across educational settings. The analysis highlights a fundamental asymmetry: while historical minority languages are institutionally recognized but internally contested (particularly with respect to standardization), languages associated with migration are largely marginalized. The paper argues that both phenomena can be understood within a broader ideological framework described as “monolingualism within multilingualism”, and calls for a rethinking of language education policies in Italy.
doi:10.3390/languages11080170.title: Historical and New Minority Languages in Italian Educational Contexts: Practices, Challenges, and Ideologies

doi:10.3390/make8080246.abstract: Target-speaker automatic speech recognition (TS-ASR) enables transcription of a specific speaker in multi-talker environments, yet remains largely unexplored for multilingual, low-resource languages. Existing TS-ASR systems predominantly target monolingual English using diarization-based or speaker-embedding approaches, leaving a critical gap for languages such as Kazakh, where code-switching with Russian and English is commonplace. We propose Persona-ASR, a modular two-stage architecture. The first stage is an explicit target-presence gate that verifies whether the enrolled speaker appears in the mixture and emits a token to suppress transcription when the speaker is absent, directly addressing the acoustic-hallucination failure mode of prior systems. The second stage performs enrollment-conditioned recognition: a 192-dimensional ECAPA-TDNN speaker embedding modulates a WavLM-Base-Plus encoder through feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), while language-specific CTC heads enable joint Kazakh and English decoding without forcing Latin and Cyrillic symbols to compete in a single output space. To evaluate the system, we introduce KazMix3, a Kazakh overlap dataset for TS-ASR training, and PersonaMix, a controlled bilingual benchmark spanning same- and cross-language enrollment across varying interferer counts (1–3) and signal-to-noise ratios (−3 to +3 dB). Persona-ASR outperforms a strong off-the-shelf cascade baseline by 13.3 WER points on English and 24.6 on Kazakh, and matches a published monolingual English baseline. On PersonaMix, speaker conditioning reduces relative word error rate by 40.7% on English and 59.3% on Kazakh mixtures over an unconditioned variant of the same model, and cross-language enrollment (unseen during training) remains effective, increasing average raw WER by only 4.1 points (English) and 2.2 points (Kazakh) relative to same-language enrollment. To our knowledge, Persona-ASR is the first TS-ASR system for the Kazakh language, establishing a foundation for multilingual personalized ASR in low-resource settings.
doi:10.3390/make8080246.title: Persona-ASR: Bilingual Target-Speaker Speech Recognition for Kazakh–English Overlapping Speech

doi:10.34044/j.kjss.2026.47.3.18.abstract: Students in Indonesia must complete the study of regional languages as their mother tongue learning. Regional languages for students are considered difficult because of inadequate teaching materials, especially Using (Osing) language teaching materials for elementary school students. This study is an analysis of the need to determine the foundation to be used in the development of teaching material products in elementary school in Banyuwangi, East Java, Indonesia. This study used convergent parallel mixed method and qualitative approach to conduct surveys and interviews for data analysis. The results showed that students need teaching materials Using (Osing) regional languages for mother tongue learning. Analyze student needs by pointing out eight things: who the language learner is, proficiency level, intercultural competence, learning preferences, attitudes, goals and expectations, target context, and student interests. Meanwhile, four things for teachers ‘ needs are related to problems and identifying priorities facing teachers, identifying abilities, identifying attitudes, and solutions. These results will be the basis for the development of Using (Osing) language teaching materials for elementary school students in Indonesia.
doi:10.34044/j.kjss.2026.47.3.18.title: Need analysis on developing Using (Osing) teaching material as a mother tongue learning in Indonesia

doi:10.34778/a48xn206.abstract: Brief Description This variable proposes LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection (see also Bommarito & Michael, 2025; Liang et al., 2026) and refers to the automated identification, contextual interpretation, and measurement of dialectal, vernacular, or otherwise non-standard linguistic forms in digital texts (Joshi et al., 2025). The procedure combines dictionary-based detection with large language model (LLM)-assisted contextual glossing. A gloss is understood here as a standardized explanation or rendering of a dialectal expression that supports computational analysis while preserving the original linguistic form (Bommarito & Michael, 2025). The variable operationalizes dialect use by identifying vernacular tokens, phrases, or grammatical forms and converting these observations into measurable outputs. One output is dialect intensity, calculated either as a continuous measure, such as the number or proportion of dialect markers per comment, post, or document, or as an ordinal measure, such as low, medium, or high dialect presence. Additional outputs may include glossed text, lists of detected dialect terms, uncertainty scores (provided by the model), and dialect dictionaries developed from corpus-level aggregation. For instance, the comment “cah even scratch my bamcee in peace inno” contains three detected dialect forms: cah, bamcee, and inno. These are contextually glossed as “I can't even scratch my behind in peace, you know,” while the original wording is retained for analysis. Based on the proportion and distribution of detected dialect forms, the comment receives a dialect intensity score of 0.38. LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection is particularly relevant for automated content analysis in dialect-rich environments where standard preprocessing pipelines may normalize, misclassify, or erase vernacular forms. In such contexts, spelling variation, code-switching, phonetic writing, regional grammar, and culturally specific vocabulary can reduce the validity of downstream analyses such as sentiment analysis, topic modeling, stance detection, or frame analysis. The original text remains unchanged, while the gloss layer provides a machine-readable representation for subsequent automated analysis. While low-resource language glossing is fairly successful if the model is provided with sufficient context, the approach should be combined with a human/machine-in-the-loop approach to avoid reintroducing the language-flattening aspects of automated translation that this approach aims to avoid (Alqazlan et al., 2025; Hong et al., 2022). Field of Application/Theoretical Foundation The theoretical foundation of the variable lies in sociolinguistic work on language variation, indexicality, and the social meaning of dialect (Eckert, 2008; Labov, 1972). Vernacular forms can signal locality, group membership, stance, affect, humor, intimacy, resistance, or cultural belonging (Ming, 2020). At the same time, the variable is grounded in computational communication research and automated content analysis. Dictionary-based procedures are widely used but depend on the quality and coverage of the underlying dictionary. This is problematic in dialect-rich contexts, where relevant terms may be absent from standard dictionaries, may appear in multiple spellings, or may only be interpretable within local context. LLM-assisted glossing can help address these limitations by identifying additional candidate forms and producing contextual metadata. References/Combination with other Methods of Data Collection LLM-Assisted Dialect Gloss Detection can be combined with manual content analysis or serve as a preprocessing step for other automated content analysis variables. For example, sentiment analysis may be conducted on both the original text and the glossed text to examine whether dialect-aware preprocessing changes sentiment scores. Topic modeling or frame analysis may be applied after glossing to reduce the exclusion of dialect-rich comments from interpretable topic clusters. A typical automated procedure consists of the following steps: Corpus preparation: Collect digital texts and retain the original text without normalization or spelling correction. Seed dictionary construction: Develop an initial vernacular dictionary from existing linguistic resources, prior research, expert knowledge, or manually reviewed corpus samples. Dictionary-based detection: Identify known dialect tokens or phrases through rule-based or dictionary-based matching. LLM-assisted glossing: Use constrained prompts to identify additional dialect forms, propose contextual glosses, and generate structured metadata. Human validation: Review a benchmark sample of extracted terms and glosses, ideally with coders or validators familiar with the relevant language variety. Validators assess whether the extracted forms are contextually valid, whether the glosses accurately represent their meaning, and whether cultural meaning, pragmatic force, and the voice of the original comment have been preserved. Disagreements or inaccurate outputs are used to revise the dictionary, glosses, and prompting procedure. External sources, including published online and offline dictionaries are used as external validators. Dictionary refinement: Terms are shown to validators in batches of 25 to confirm Add validated forms to the dictionary and remove false positives. Scoring: Calculate dialect intensity as a raw count, normalized rate, binary indicator, or ordinal category, e.g. Downstream analysis: Use the original and glossed text for further automated or qualitative analysis. Example Studies for Automated Content Analysis Table 1 provides examples of work on dialect detection in low resource languages. Robinson et al. (2024) introduce Kreyòl-MT, a large-scale machine-translation dataset and model infrastructure for Creole languages across Latin America, the Caribbean, and Africa. Smith et al. (2026) develop CariBOT, a Trinidadian English Creole to Standard English architecture for improving chatbot responses. Their Caribe library preprocesses Creole input before it reaches a standard English chatbot. Jackson et al. (2025) assess GPT-4’s communicative competence with Trinidadian English Creole and show the struggle with vocabulary, authenticity, and correct identification. doi:10.35307/saltel.v9i2.183.abstract: The characteristics of social media influencers (charismatic personas, storytelling, humour and the use of layman’s terms) have increasingly permeated into higher education, but there has been little empirical research on how the delivery of social media influencers influences the attitudes of students in formal university setting, especially in Southeast Asian settings. The study investigates the attitudes of university students towards the use of influencer’s pedagogical style, based on Petty and Cacioppo’s (1986) Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), which distinguishes between the academic content quality (central route) and the stylistic/persona cues (peripheral route). A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was conducted on a convenience sample of 120 students (70 from Brunei Darussalam and 50 from Bandung, Indonesia) with five-point Likert scales and analysed with SPSS with Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression and independent samples t-text. The reliability of all constructs was very high (α = .908 – .951) The results showed that there was a strong and positive correlation between content quality and attitudes (r = .860) and also between stylistic/persona cues and attitudes (r = .796). The overall model accounted 80.2% of the variance in attitude, with content quality being the more powerful predictor (β = .597) and stylistic/persona cues being a significant independent predictor (β = .363). A significant difference in positive attitudes was found between the Indonesian (M – 3.83) and Bruneian (M = 3.51) respondents. Lastly, the study suggests that the influence-pedagogy approach combine intellectual rigour with entertaining presentations and be applied culturally appropriate to each country’s higher education system.
doi:10.35307/saltel.v9i2.183.journal_ref: SALTeL Journal (Southeast Asia Language Teaching and Learning)

doi:10.35314/annm4j49.abstract: Regional languages and scripts, including the Melayu Ogan script, face the threat of extinction due to declining usage and limited digital documentation in the modern era. While current Indonesian script research primarily focuses on popular scripts, research addressing the Ogan Malay script remains severely limited. To address this gap, this study provides one of the earliest implementations of the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) VGG-19 architecture specifically designed for Ogan Malay script classification. This research utilises a primary dataset provided by the Language Center of South Sumatra Province, consisting of 185 distinct character classes, with each class initially containing one original image. The VGG-19 architecture is applied and supported by data augmentation techniques to enrich spatial variability, followed by evaluation using k-fold cross validation. Evaluation results demonstrate excellent classification performance. The model achieved maximum convergence without any indications of overfitting at an optimal configuration of 30 epochs with a learning rate of 0.0001. This configuration successfully resulted in an accuracy of 99.14%, a precision of 0.9870, a recall of 0.9914, and an F1-score of 0.9885. The success of this classification model provides a strong foundation for future real-time regional script recognition applications to support cultural preservation.
doi:10.35314/annm4j49.title: Implementation of a Convolutional Neural Network Using VGG19 for Ogan Malay Script Recognition

doi:10.35320/ij.207.abstract: Metadata describing legacy television broadcasts in archival collections is often incomplete or inconsistent, but additional information about the program content and contributors can be recovered from on-screen text. Leveraging this information requires text extraction, and the accuracy of this process is crucial for enhancing metadata quality and discoverability in television archives. Despite recent advances in AI offering improved extraction of text from visual data, statistical models still perform worse on data that differs from their training data. Therefore, the new models may underperform when interpreting names that are underrepresented in language corpora. This article investigates algorithmic understanding of scenes with text from television programs, contrasting Hawaiian lower third text from PBS Hawaiʻi broadcasts with comparable text from public television programs broadcast in the continental United States. Our primary research question is whether distinctive names (such as those of Hawaiian and Japanese origin), distinctive orthography, and complex visual features (as with leis or Hawaiian shirts) impact accuracy of text transcription. To address this question, we compiled a dataset of almost 4,000 still images from television broadcasts, split between PBS Hawaiʻi and stations from the continental United States, to evaluate multiple OCR and NLP systems, including traditional OCR approaches, as well as larger vision-language models. We find that although Hawaiian on-screen text does not result in significantly lower transcription accuracy overall than for on-screen text from the continental United States, distinctive features of Hawaiian content disproportionately cause errors. Based on these findings, we discuss implications for applying general purpose AI tools to local collections with distinctive characteristics.
doi:10.35320/ij.207.journal_ref: International Association of Sound and Audiovisual Archives (IASA) Journal

glossary.explanation_id: Teks yang muncul di sepertiga bagian bawah layar televisi untuk mengidentifikasi pembicara atau menyediakan informasi kontekstual.
*Model* kecerdasan buatan end-to-end yang mengintegrasikan pemahaman visual dan linguistik untuk memproses gambar dan teks secara bersamaan.
*Metrik* yang mengukur minimum jumlah penyuntingan tingkat karakter yang diperlukan untuk mengubah teks prediksi menjadi teks referensi yang sebenarnya.
*Metrik* biner yang bernilai satu jika teks prediksi identik dengan data referensi dan bernilai nol jika berbeda.
Tanda diakritik seperti makron atau tanda henti glotal yang ditambahkan pada huruf untuk mengubah pelafalan atau arti kata.

background.en: Metadata describing legacy television broadcasts in archival collections is frequently incomplete or inconsistent, making archival content difficult to search and discover. Additional program information and contributor details can be recovered from on-screen text, particularly lower third chyrons that identify speakers. However, extracting text from legacy video footage poses significant technical and sociotechnical challenges, such as signal degradation and the underrepresentation of local naming conventions in training data.
background.id: Metadata yang mendeskripsikan siaran televisi warisan dalam koleksi arsip seringkali tidak lengkap atau tidak konsisten, membuat konten arsip sulit dicari dan ditemukan. Informasi program tambahan dan detail kontributor dapat dipulihkan dari teks pada layar, terutama *chyron* *lower third* yang mengidentifikasi pembicara. Namun, mengekstrak teks dari rekaman video lama menimbulkan tantangan teknis dan sosioteknis yang signifikan, seperti degradasi sinyal dan kurang terwakilinya konvensi penamaan lokal dalam *training data*.

contributions.en: This paper contributes a curated dataset of nearly 4,000 still images extracted from 289 public television episodes, balanced between PBS Hawaii and continental US broadcasts across different eras. It provides a systematic evaluation of traditional OCR pipelines and state-of-the-art vision-language models on text extraction under complex visual conditions and distinct linguistic origins.
contributions.id: Makalah ini menyumbangkan *dataset* terkurasi yang terdiri dari hampir 4.000 gambar diam yang diekstrak dari 289 episode televisi publik, seimbang antara siaran PBS Hawaii dan AS kontinental di berbagai era. Makalah ini memberikan *evaluasi* sistematis terhadap *pipeline* *OCR* tradisional dan *vision-language model* mutakhir pada ekstraksi teks dalam kondisi visual yang kompleks dan asal linguistik yang berbeda.

future_work.en: The authors note that their dataset can serve as a basis for named entity recognition and named entity linking systems. Future research could explore domain-specific fine-tuning of vision-language models on broadcast chyron data to improve accuracy and investigate multimodal fusion methods combining audio transcripts with visual extraction.
future_work.id: Para penulis mencatat bahwa *dataset* mereka dapat berfungsi sebagai dasar untuk sistem *named entity recognition* dan *named entity linking*. Penelitian masa depan dapat mengeksplorasi *fine-tuning* khusus domain pada *vision-language model* menggunakan data *chyron* siaran untuk meningkatkan akurasi dan menyelidiki metode *multimodal fusion* yang menggabungkan transkrip audio dengan ekstraksi visual.

method.en: The authors compiled 3,922 still images split between a Hawaiian set and a continental US comparison set, matching visual styles across old and new eras. They performed manual transcriptions and additional labelings for visual features such as leis, Hawaiian shirts, and opaque graphics, alongside AI-assisted and human-verified name origins for Hawaiian and Japanese names. They evaluated three systems: docTR as a traditional OCR baseline, SmolVLM2 2.2B Instruct, and DeepSeek-OCR, using case-normalized Character Error Rate and Exact Match accuracy.
method.id: Para penulis menyusun 3.922 gambar diam yang dibagi menjadi set Hawaii dan set pembanding AS kontinental, mencocokkan gaya visual di era lama dan baru. Mereka melakukan transkripsi manual dan pelabelan tambahan untuk fitur visual seperti lei, kemeja Hawaii, dan grafik buram, beserta asal nama yang dibantu AI dan diverifikasi manusia untuk nama Hawaii dan Jepang. Mereka mengevaluasi tiga sistem: docTR sebagai *baseline* *OCR* tradisional, SmolVLM2 2.2B Instruct, dan DeepSeek-OCR, dengan menggunakan *Character Error Rate* yang dinormalisasi hurufnya dan akurasi *Exact Match*.

related_work.en: Prior research in broadcast video processing includes automated transcription followed by text analysis at the Vanderbilt Television News Archive and real-time OCR on contemporary news streams via projects like GDELT and the Internet Archive's Third Eye. While these initiatives successfully process modern, clean, born-digital content, older broadcast footage captured on analog tape or film suffers from visual artifacts, noise, and color distortion that render standard OCR methods less effective.
related_work.id: Penelitian sebelumnya dalam pemrosesan video siaran mencakup transkripsi otomatis yang diikuti oleh analisis teks di Vanderbilt Television News Archive serta *OCR* waktu nyata pada aliran berita kontemporer melalui proyek-proyek seperti GDELT dan Third Eye dari Internet Archive. Meskipun inisiatif ini berhasil memproses konten digital modern yang bersih, rekaman siaran lama yang ditangkap pada pita analog atau film mengalami artefak visual, derau, dan distorsi warna yang membuat metode *OCR* standar kurang efektif.

results.en: The results demonstrate a clear performance hierarchy where SmolVLM2 outperformed DeepSeek-OCR, which in turn significantly outperformed docTR across the full dataset. Although geographic origin alone did not degrade accuracy, specific features such as Hawaiian proper names and visual complexity like flowers and leis caused measurable drops in transcription performance across models.
results.id: Hasil penelitian menunjukkan hierarki performa yang jelas di mana SmolVLM2 mengungguli DeepSeek-OCR, yang pada gilirannya jauh mengungguli docTR pada keseluruhan *dataset*. Meskipun asal geografis saja tidak menurunkan akurasi, fitur khusus seperti nama diri Hawaii dan kompleksitas visual seperti bunga dan lei menyebabkan penurunan yang terukur dalam performa transkripsi di seluruh model.

tldr.en: This paper investigates how vision-language models and traditional OCR systems transcribe television chyrons from PBS Hawaii compared to continental US broadcasts. The results show that while overall geographic origin does not degrade accuracy, distinctive features like Hawaiian proper names and complex visual backgrounds disproportionately cause transcription errors.
tldr.id: Makalah ini menyelidiki bagaimana *vision-language model* dan sistem *OCR* tradisional mentranskripsikan *chyron* televisi dari PBS Hawaii dibandingkan siaran AS kontinental. Hasilnya menunjukkan bahwa meskipun asal geografis secara keseluruhan tidak menurunkan akurasi, fitur khas seperti nama diri Hawaii dan latar belakang visual yang kompleks secara tidak proporsional menyebabkan kesalahan transkripsi.

doi:10.35320/ij.207.title: Understanding On-Screen Text Do AI Tools Struggle with Hawaiian Chyrons?
doi:10.35320/ij.207.venue: International Association of Sound and Audiovisual Archives (IASA) Journal

doi:10.35882/ijeeemi.v8i3.327.abstract: Indonesian healthcare question-answering (QA) systems often operate in low-resource settings and must handle substantial linguistic variability in real-world user queries, including paraphrasing, informal expressions, and implicit intent. These challenges are compounded by limited annotated healthcare data and the diverse ways patients express similar medical needs in everyday language, causing QA models to rely heavily on surface-level wording. This study proposes a new multi-stage data augmentation method to improve the robustness of a healthcare chatbot based on IndoBERT Fine-Tuned. The proposed method integrates domain-specific fine-tuning with an augmentation pipeline that introduces paraphrased question variants with IndoT5, normalizes informal language, and incorporates controlled lexical variation through Part-of-Speech (POS) based verb synonym replacement while preserving medical entities, thereby expanding linguistic coverage without requiring additional manual annotation. The augmentation process preserves medical intent while generating diverse surface forms, enabling the model to learn more flexible representations of user queries. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed multi-stage augmentation substantially improves the robustness of the IndoBERT-based healthcare question answering system. Full augmentation expands the training data to 1,424 question–answer pairs and achieves 67.37 Exact Match (EM) and 85.59 F1. Compared with training without augmentation, this corresponds to relative improvements of approximately 11.8% in EM and 7.0% in F1, indicating more reliable answer span extraction under paraphrased, informal, and lexically varied queries. These gains reflect improved alignment between conversational user input and structured healthcare information. Overall, this work highlights the importance of integrated data augmentation for enhancing low-resource Indonesian healthcare question-answering systems. By exposing the model to broader linguistic variations during training, the proposed approach supports more stable real-world performance while maintaining medical intent consistency and provides insights into remaining challenges for reliable healthcare QA deployment.
doi:10.35882/ijeeemi.v8i3.327.journal_ref: Indonesian Journal of Electronics Electromedical Engineering and Medical Informatics

glossary.explanation_id: Tugas *NLP* di mana model harus mengekstrak rentang teks jawaban yang tepat langsung dari konteks yang diberikan.
Teknik memperluas ukuran dan keragaman *korpus* pelatihan dengan menghasilkan data sintesis secara otomatis.
Proses melatih ulang model bahasa praterlatih pada *dataset* domain khusus tertentu untuk tugas downstream.
Metrik *evaluasi* yang mengukur apakah prediksi model cocok secara persis dengan teks jawaban sebenarnya.
Analisis sistematis di mana komponen tertentu dari model atau *pipeline* dihapus secara bergantian untuk mengukur kontribusinya.
Klasifikasi kata ke dalam kategori gramatikal dasarnya seperti nomina, verba, atau adjektiva.
Kondisi di mana ketersediaan data beranotasi atau sumber daya komputasi untuk suatu bahasa sangat terbatas.
Simbol sementara yang digunakan untuk menggantikan entitas penting selama pemrosesan agar tidak rusak.

background.en: Indonesian healthcare question-answering systems often operate in low-resource settings and must handle substantial linguistic variability in patient queries, including paraphrasing, informal expressions, and lexical variation. Limited annotated healthcare data further restricts QA models' ability to generalize beyond surface-level wording, necessitating robust methods to improve chatbot performance.
background.id: Sistem *question-answering* kesehatan berbahasa Indonesia sering beroperasi pada pengaturan *low-resource* dan harus menangani variabilitas linguistik yang substansial dalam kueri pasien, termasuk parafrase, ekspresi informal, dan variasi leksikal. Keterbatasan data kesehatan beranotasi semakin membatasi kemampuan model *QA* untuk menggeneralisasi di luar kata-kata tingkat permukaan, sehingga memerlukan metode yang handal untuk meningkatkan performa *chatbot*.

contributions.en: This study proposes a medically-aware, multi-stage data augmentation pipeline for an IndoBERT-based hospital chatbot. The novel contributions include medical-term protection using placeholder-based masking to prevent semantic distortion, staged augmentation through optional slang normalization, IndoT5-based paraphrasing, and POS-guided verb synonym replacement, evaluated under limited data conditions.
contributions.id: Studi ini mengusulkan *pipeline* *data augmentation* bertingkat yang sadar secara medis untuk *chatbot* rumah sakit berbasis IndoBERT. Kontribusi baru mencakup perlindungan istilah medis menggunakan *masking* berbasis *placeholder* untuk mencegah distorsi semantik, *augmentation* bertingkat melalui normalisasi *slang* opsional, parafrase berbasis IndoT5, dan penggantian sinonim verba yang dipandu oleh *POS*, yang dievaluasi di bawah kondisi data terbatas.

future_work.en: Future work should explore explicit intent modeling, external knowledge integration, and context-aware conversational reasoning, as well as evaluation on external datasets and real-world healthcare queries to assess generalizability, deployment readiness, and safety.
future_work.id: Penelitian masa depan harus mengeksplorasi pemodelan intens eksplisit, integrasi pengetahuan eksternal, dan penalaran percakapan yang sadar konteks, serta evaluasi pada *dataset* eksternal dan kueri kesehatan dunia nyata untuk menilai generalisasi, kesiapan penerapan, dan keamanan.

method.en: The input dataset consists of 730 Indonesian QA pairs covering 15 hospital service intents, split into 584 training and 146 testing pairs. The pipeline processes questions through medical term masking, optional slang normalization, space and punctuation normalization, IndoT5-based paraphrasing with fallback synonym substitution, and marker restoration. The augmented dataset is merged with the original data to fine-tune an extractive question-answering IndoBERT model using the AdamW optimizer and standard cross-validation practices.
method.id: Dataset masukan terdiri dari 730 pasangan *QA* bahasa Indonesia yang mencakup 15 intens layanan rumah sakit, dibagi menjadi 584 pasangan pelatihan dan 146 pasangan pengujian. *Pipeline* memproses pertanyaan melalui *masking* istilah medis, normalisasi *slang* opsional, normalisasi spasi dan tanda baca, parafrase berbasis IndoT5 dengan substitusi sinonim *fallback*, dan pemulihan penanda. *Dataset* yang diaugmentasi digabungkan dengan data asli untuk melakukan *fine-tuning* pada model IndoBERT *extractive question-answering* menggunakan pengoptimal AdamW dan praktik *cross-validation* standar.

related_work.en: Previous studies have explored data augmentation techniques such as Modified Easy Data Augmentation, Knowledge Mixture Data Augmentation, and morphology-based augmentation using Indonesian affixes to address limited dataset availability. However, such generic approaches often fail to balance sample diversity with label consistency, and prior strategies have been less explored for Indonesian healthcare question answering containing informal language and domain-specific medical terms.
related_work.id: Studi sebelumnya telah mengeksplorasi teknik *data augmentation* seperti *Modified Easy Data Augmentation*, *Knowledge Mixture Data Augmentation*, dan *augmentation* berbasis morfologi menggunakan afiks bahasa Indonesia untuk mengatasi keterbatasan ketersediaan *dataset*. Namun, pendekatan generik tersebut sering gagal menyeimbangkan keragaman sampel dengan konsistensi label, dan strategi sebelumnya masih kurang dieksplorasi untuk *question-answering* kesehatan berbahasa Indonesia yang mengandung bahasa informal serta istilah medis spesifik domain.

results.en: Experimental results demonstrate that full augmentation achieves 68.22% Exact Match and 82.06% F1, representing relative improvements of 13.2% in EM and 2.6% in F1 over the non-augmented baseline. An ablation study reveals that removing slang normalization yields the highest performance at 69.59% EM and 85.21% F1, suggesting that preserving informal expressions better reflects real-world patient queries.
results.id: Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa *augmentation* penuh mencapai 68,22% *Exact Match* dan 82,06% F1, yang merepresentasikan peningkatan relatif sebesar 13,2% pada *EM* dan 2,6% pada F1 dibandingkan *baseline* tanpa *augmentation*. Studi ablasi mengungkapkan bahwa menghapus normalisasi *slang* menghasilkan performa tertinggi pada 69,59% *EM* dan 85,21% F1, menyarankan bahwa melestarikan ekspresi informal lebih mencerminkan kueri pasien di dunia nyata.

tldr.en: This study proposes a multi-stage data augmentation method to improve the robustness of Indonesian healthcare question-answering systems under low-resource settings. Experimental results show that full augmentation significantly enhances Exact Match and F1 scores over non-augmented baselines.
tldr.id: Studi ini mengusulkan metode *data augmentation* bertingkat untuk meningkatkan ketahanan sistem *question-answering* kesehatan berbahasa Indonesia pada pengaturan *low-resource*. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa *augmentation* penuh secara signifikan meningkatkan skor *Exact Match* dan F1 dibandingkan *baseline* tanpa *augmentation*.

doi:10.35961/salee.v7i2.2920.abstract: This study examined the association between informal digital learning of English (IDLE) activities and willingness to communicate in a second language (L2 WTC) in three distinct communicative contexts: in-class, out-of-class, and extramural digital contexts. A quantitative research method with a correlation design was adopted. A total of 318 Indonesian undergraduate EFL students from four different faculties at one state Islamic university in Central Java participated in an online survey upon invitation. Jamovi 2.2.5 was used to perform statistical computations regarding the reliability test of instruments, the generation of descriptive statistics results, Pearson correlation analysis, and linear regression analysis. The results showed that the students were more engaged in receptive IDLE activities (RIA) than in productive IDLE activities (PIA), although the mean values of both RIA and PIA did not exceed 3.00. In contrast, the mean value of L2 WTC exceeded 3.00, suggesting that the students were generally willing to communicate in English. Regarding correlation, both RIA and PIA were positively associated with L2 WTC. RIA significantly predicted students’ L2 WTC, whereas PIA did not. RIA also explained 15% of the total variance in L2 WTC. This implies that, despite their considerable L2 WTC, students should still utilize digital devices to learn English in extramural digital contexts. Leveraging their enjoyment of PIA, particularly interaction-based PIA, is crucial for promoting two-way communication skills, ultimately benefiting L2 WTC.

doi:10.36040/jati.v10i4.18599.abstract: Prediksi penjualan merupakan aspek penting dalam mendukung pengambilan keputusan bisnis, khususnya dalam pengelolaan stok produk terlaris. CV. Gorontalo Computer masih menghadapi kendala dalam menentukan produk yang berpotensi laris karena proses analisis penjualan dilakukan secara manual dan belum berbasis data. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengimplementasikan algoritma regresi linear sederhana dalam memprediksi penjualan produk berdasarkan data historis perusahaan. Metode yang digunakan adalah pendekatan data mining terhadap data penjualan periode Januari 2022 hingga Mei 2025, dengan tahapan preprocessing, pemodelan, dan evaluasi. Proses analisis dilakukan menggunakan tiga tools, yaitu Microsoft Excel, RapidMiner, dan SPSS, untuk membandingkan konsistensi hasil dan kinerja model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa variabel periode waktu tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap jumlah penjualan pada seluruh kategori produk, dengan nilai signifikansi lebih besar dari 0,05 dan nilai R-Square yang rendah. Evaluasi menggunakan Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) menunjukkan bahwa kategori laptop memiliki tingkat kesalahan terendah, sedangkan kategori aksesoris memiliki kesalahan tertinggi. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, dapat disimpulkan bahwa algoritma regresi linear sederhana kurang optimal digunakan untuk prediksi penjualan pada CV. Gorontalo Computer
doi:10.36040/jati.v10i4.18599.title: PREDIKSI PENJUALAN PRODUK TERLARIS PADA CV. GORONTALO COMPUTER MENGGUNAKAN ALGORITMA REGRESI LINEAR

doi:10.36040/jati.v10i4.18816.abstract: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh meningkatnya jumlah berita pada platform Fakta Nusantara di Balai Pemasyarakatan (BAPAS) Surakarta yang belum didukung oleh sistem rekomendasi otomatis. Permasalahan yang terjadi adalah pengguna masih mengalami kesulitan dalam menemukan berita yang relevan karena proses pencarian informasi belum optimal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan mengimplementasikan sistem rekomendasi berita menggunakan metode Content-Based Filtering agar informasi yang ditampilkan lebih sesuai dengan kebutuhan pengguna. Metode yang digunakan meliputi pengumpulan data berita dari Firebase Firestore, preprocessing teks, ekstraksi fitur menggunakan TF-IDF, serta perhitungan kemiripan antar berita menggunakan Cosine Similarity. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem mampu menghasilkan rekomendasi berita berdasarkan kesamaan konten berupa judul, kategori, dan isi berita. Nilai similarity digunakan sebagai dasar perangkingan untuk menentukan berita yang paling relevan. Dengan demikian, sistem rekomendasi yang dibangun dapat membantu pengguna menemukan informasi secara lebih cepat, tepat, dan efektif pada platform Fakta Nusantara
doi:10.36040/jati.v10i4.18816.title: SISTEM REKOMENDASI BERITA FAKTA NUSANTARA MENGGUNAKAN CONTENT-BASED FILTERING PADA BAPAS SURAKARTA

doi:10.36080/skanika.v9i2.3830.abstract: Indonesia memiliki 235,26 juta pengguna internet dengan tingkat penetrasi 81,72% pada 2026, sementara ujaran kebencian mengancam kohesi sosial masyarakat majemuk. Berdasarkan literatur yang ditelaah dalam penelitian ini, belum ditemukan studi yang melakukan benchmark tiga-arah MNB, CNB, dan SVM dengan ablation study preprocessing, uji McNemar, dan analisis error Wilson CI pada konteks hate speech bahasa Indonesia. Penelitian ini mengusulkan kerangka komparatif menggunakan dataset 13.169 tweet, penanganan imbalanced class per-algoritma (SMOTE untuk MNB/CNB; CSL dan Lexicon-Based Coefficient Override untuk SVM), serta ablasi enam konfigurasi preprocessing. Hasil: MNB mencapai F1 Macro 72,10% dan Recall Abusive tertinggi (84,30%), sementara SVM mencapai Recall Abusive 80,20% dengan latensi inferensi 0,10 ms pada CPU; perbandingan langsung dengan IndoBERT pada GPU T4 tidak sepenuhnya setara lintas-perangkat-keras, namun pengukuran tambahan pada CPU yang sama menunjukkan IndoBERT berlatensi ~102,4 ms (rasio ~1.020×). Uji McNemar mengkonfirmasi perbedaan SVM vs MNB/CNB signifikan (p<0,0001), CNB vs MNB tidak signifikan (p=0,0704), mengindikasikan interaksi negatif SMOTE×CNB pada dataset dan konfigurasi penelitian ini. SVM dipilih sebagai model deployment berdasarkan Utility Score (81,39) pada skenario bobot yang diuji, dan dapat menjadi alat bantu penyaringan awal (bukan pengganti verifikasi manusia) pada platform yang beroperasi di bawah regulasi UU ITE No. 1/2024.

doi:10.36341/rabit.v11i2.8340.abstract: Sistem Isyarat Bahasa Indonesia (SIBI) merupakan media komunikasi yang digunakan oleh penyandang tunarungu di Indonesia. Namun, proses klasifikasi citra alfabet SIBI masih menghadapi kendala berupa kemiripan bentuk isyarat antarhuruf dan keterbatasan variasi data pelatihan. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengoptimalkan klasifikasi citra alfabet SIBI menggunakan augmentasi data dan fine-tuning MobileNetV2. Dataset yang digunakan berjumlah 7.582 citra alfabet SIBI yang terdiri dari 24 kelas alfabet SIBI, yaitu A sampai Y tanpa huruf J dan Z, dan diperoleh dari Kaggle. Tahapan penelitian meliputi preprocessing, augmentasi data, pembagian dataset menjadi data training, validation, dan testing, pembangunan model menggunakan transfer learning MobileNetV2, serta evaluasi menggunakan accuracy, precision, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model tanpa augmentasi memperoleh akurasi 96,75%, sedangkan model dengan augmentasi memperoleh akurasi 97,10% disertai peningkatan nilai precision, recall, dan F1-score. Hasil penelitian memperlihatkan bahwa augmentasi data mampu meningkatkan kemampuan generalisasi model sehingga menghasilkan klasifikasi yang lebih akurat dan konsisten. Dengan demikian, kombinasi augmentasi data dan fine-tuning MobileNetV2 efektif digunakan untuk klasifikasi citra alfabet SIBI. Uji McNemar menunjukkan adanya perbedaan performa model yang signifikan secara statistik setelah penerapan augmentasi data (p = 9,6517 × 10⁻¹²).

doi:10.36341/rabit.v11i2.8370.abstract: Perguruan tinggi swasta menghadapi tantangan dalam memahami pergeseran karakteristik calon mahasiswa akibat dinamika sosial-ekonomi, termasuk pandemi COVID-19. ITSNU Pekalongan mencatat pola pendaftaran tidak linear selama 2019–2024 (146 hingga puncak 680; total 2.362 data). Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis segmentasi probabilistik, mengukur structural break antarperiode, membangun otomasi analisis berbasis large language model (LLM), dan menguji validitasnya melalui expert judgement. Metode Research and Development mengikuti CRISP-DM sepuluh tahap: IndoBERT (768 dimensi), PCA, Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) dengan covariance diag dan init k-means++, Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), serta Hybrid Cognitive Pipeline (Llama 3.2 lokal dan OpenRouter cloud). Hasil menunjukkan 4 dari 5 transisi terkonfirmasi sebagai structural break (ARI < 0,30), cosine similarity antarentitas identik embedding IndoBERT rata-rata 0,9234 (kisaran 0,8932–0,9426), dan validasi pakar 4,0/5,0 untuk proyeksi 592 pendaftar tahun 2025. Integrasi IndoBERT–GMM–LLM menghasilkan sistem pendukung keputusan rekrutmen yang dapat direplikasi setiap tahun akademik.

doi:10.36341/rabit.v11i2.8498.abstract: Klasifikasi sentimen pada teks media sosial berbahasa Indonesia masih menjadi tantangan karena ejaan informal, pencampuran kode bahasa, ekspresi budaya yang spesifik, dan ketidakseimbangan kelas dapat mengurangi reliabilitas model. Dengan menggunakan kumpulan data berisi 1.336 postingan X berlabel terkait Pemilihan Presiden Indonesia tahun 2024, penelitian ini membandingkan dua alur kerja transformer untuk klasifikasi sentimen tiga kelas, yaitu fine-tuning IndoBERT pada teks bahasa Indonesia dan alur kerja berbasis terjemahan, di mana NLLB-200 menerjemahkan teks yang sama ke dalam bahasa Inggris sebelum proses pelatihan RoBERTa. Kumpulan data tersebut dibagi melalui pengambilan sampel bertingkat menjadi 1.069 contoh pelatihan, 133 contoh validasi, dan 134 contoh pengujian. Kedua model tersebut dilatih selama lima epoch dengan pengaturan optimisasi yang sama dan dievaluasi menggunakan akurasi, presisi berbobot, recall berbobot, F1-score berbobot, skor per kelas, dan confusion matrix. IndoBERT mencapai akurasi 82,09% dan F1 berbobot 80,31%, dibandingkan dengan 80,60% dan 75,69% untuk pipeline NLLB-200 plus RoBERTa. Perbedaan terbesar terjadi pada kelas netral, di mana IndoBERT memperoleh nilai recall sebesar 0,26 sedangkan RoBERTa hanya 0,05. Analisis tingkat kesalahan menunjukkan bahwa artefak terjemahan dan bias kelas mayoritas secara bersama-sama mengurangi sensitivitas terhadap ekspresi netral dan ekspresi yang bergantung pada konteks. Penyesuaian monolingual secara langsung terbukti lebih efektif untuk dataset ini, meskipun teknik transfer berbasis terjemahan tetap kompetitif untuk kelas positif yang dominan. Penelitian selanjutnya sebaiknya menggunakan dataset yang lebih besar dan dianotasi secara independen, pengulangan uji coba, analisis kualitas terjemahan, serta tujuan pelatihan yang mempertimbangkan pengelompokan kelas.

doi:10.36378/jps.v8i2.5280.abstract: Desa Pulau Banjar Kari merupakan salah satu desa yang ada di Kecamatan Kuantan Tengah, Kabupaten Kuantan Singingi. Desa Pulau Banjar Kari terdiri dari 6 RT, 2 RW, dan 2 Dusun. Desa Pulau Banjar Kari memiliki potensi wilayah berupa permukiman, fasilitas umum, serta jaringan jalan desa. Namun, hingga saat ini ketersediaan data spasial desa yang terintegrasi masih terbatas sehingga menyulitkan pemerintah desa dalam perencanaan pembangunan dan pengelolaan potensi wilayah.Tujuan dari penelitian ini adalah untuk mengembangkan Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG) dalam pemetaan wilayah Desa Pulau Banjar Kari yang berada di Kecamatan Kuantan Tengah, Kabupaten Kuantan Singingi. Pemanfaatan SIG dilakukan menggunakan platform QGIS sebagai media pemetaan digital yang interaktif dan mudah diakses. Metode penelitian yang digunakan adalah metode deskriptif dengan pendekatan survei lapangan dan pengolahan data spasial. Data yang digunakan terdiri dari data primer yang diperoleh melalui observasi langsung dan wawancara dengan perangkat desa dan masyarakat desa Pulau Banjar Kari, serta data sekunder berupa peta administrasi dan dokumen pendukung. Hasil penelitian berupa peta desa yang menampilkan batas wilayah, persebaran fasilitas umum dan jaringan jalan. Peta ini diharapkan dapat menjadi sumber informasi yang akurat serta mendukung perencanaan pembangunan desa secara efektif dan berkelanjutan.
doi:10.36378/jps.v8i2.5280.title: PEMETAAN WILAYAH ADMINISTRATIF DAN INFRASTUKTUR DESA PULAU BANJAR KARI KECAMATAN KUANTAN TENGAH MENGUNAKAN INFORMASI GEOGRAFIS

doi:10.36713/epra31377.abstract: Ang pag-aaral na ito ay naglayong suriin ang antas ng kasanayan sa malikhaing pagsulat ng tula at ang kaugnayan nito sa akademikong pagganap sa asignaturang Filipino ng mga mag-aaral sa Baitang 7 hanggang Baitang 10 taong pampaaralan 2025-2026 ng Mataas na paaralan sa Hinigaran. Gamit ang deskriptib-korelasyonal na disenyo ng pananaliksik, kinalap ang datos mula sa 100 na mga mag-aaral na pinili sa pamamagitan ng random sampling. Upang masukat ang kasanayan sa pagsulat ng tula, gumamit ang mga mananaliksik ng isang pormal na rubrik na nagsuri sa larangan ng paggamit ng tayutay, sukat at tugma, orihinalidad, paggamit ng wika at organisasyon ng kaisipan. Samantala, ang akademikong pagganap ay batay sa pangkalahatang marka ng mga mag-aaral sa asignaturang Filipino.Ipinakita ng mga resulta na ang antas ng kasanayan sa malikhaing pagsulat ng tula ng mga mag-aaral ay nasa kategoryang mataas, habang ang kanilang akademikong pagganap ay nasa antas na napakahusay. Batay sa pagsusuring estadistikal gamit ang Pearson's r, natuklasang may makabuluhang kaugnayan sa pagitan ng kasanayan sa malikhaing pagsulat ng tula at ng akademikong pagganap ng mga mag-aaral. Nagpapahiwatig ito na habang tumataas ang kakayahan ng mag-aaral sa pagbuo ng tula, tumataas din ang kanilang kabuuang pagganap sa asignaturang Filipino. Batay sa mga natuklasan, inirerekomenda ng pag-aaral na ito ang patuloy na pagpapatupad ng mga interaktibo at malikhaing gawaing pampanitikan sa kurikulum upang higit pang mapalalim ang pag-unawa at interes ng mga mag-aaral sa wika at panitikang Filipino.

doi:10.36805/jh41mx81.abstract: This study successfully proposes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based model for automatic classification of Indonesian regional song lyrics by language. Unlike prior works that often focus on sentiment analysis or use unbalanced datasets, this research utilizes a balanced dataset consisting of 2,500 lyric segments from five regional languages: Javanese, Sundanese, Batak, Minangkabau, and Banjarese. A comprehensive preprocessing pipeline is applied, including case folding, text cleaning, tokenization, stopword removal, stemming, sequence padding, and label encoding to transform textual data into numerical representations. The model is evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation to ensure robustness and generalization across different data partitions. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 95.24%, precision of 95.36%, recall of 95.24%, and F1-score of 95.26%, indicating strong and consistent performance. These findings demonstrate that LSTM effectively captures sequential linguistic patterns and contextual relationships within regional languages, enabling accurate classification despite similarities in vocabulary and structure. Furthermore, this study contributes to the advancement of natural language processing for low-resource languages and highlights the potential of deep learning approaches in supporting the digital preservation and automatic organization of Indonesian regional cultural content.
